 Yet he can also show
leniency toward his
subordinates. When he
learned that Hakkotsuki's
daughter Lisa had
betrayed them, he honored
Hakkotsuki's plea not to
have to kill his own
daughter and ordered
someone else to carry out
the execution instead. He
also showed consideration
for Hidler, who had just
made a miraculous return
from the brink of death
before the final battle,
by ordering him to rest.

Emperor Bry was the
ruler of the Hyakki
Empire and possessed
powerful telepathic
abilities. The goal of the
Hyakki Empire was to
implant artificial horns
that served as telepathic
wave receiving antennas
into the heads of
humanity, transforming
them into Hyakki Soldiers
to serve as pawns in
their world conquest.
However, to efficiently
develop Hyakki Soldiers
and Hyakki mecha, they
needed a Getter Ray
amplification device, and
Bry relentlessly attacked
the Saotome Research
Institute to obtain it. He
possessed the
ruthlessness, cruelty, and
dignity expected of his
demonic appearance. All of
these surpassed even
those of Emperor Gore of
the Dinosaur Empire. Yet
he also had a lenient side
toward his subordinates;
when he learned that
Lisa, the daughter of
Hakkotsu Oni, had
betrayed them, he honored
Hakkotsu Oni's plea not
to have to kill his own
daughter and ordered
someone else to execute
her. Also, during the
final battle, he showed
consideration for Hidlar,
who had just made a
miraculous return, by
ordering him to rest. In
the end, he raised the
Science Fortress Island to
challenge the final battle,
but was defeated before
the Getter Robo.

The combat commander
who oversees the Hyakki
Empire's military might.
Along with Dr. Gura, he
serves as one of Emperor
Burai's right-hand men,
but behind the scenes he
is a scheming man with
his eye on Burai's own
position.
 Underhanded and
contemptible by nature,
he directs his malice at
ally and enemy alike. In
the past, fearing that
his position as marshal
was threatened, he framed
General Jirai and had him
executed, and when he
judged that the general's
son Jiraiki had likewise
become a threat, he
treacherously struck him
down amid the fighting.
 He is no mere petty
villain, however; he
possesses real ability,
having broken through the
barrier of the newly built
battleship Sea Force with
his personal fighter
craft, survived the
explosion of a Hyakki
robot against all odds,
and even taken Hayato
prisoner while making his
escape.

Marshal Hidlar was the
battle commander in
charge of the military
forces of the Hyakki
Empire. He worked
alongside Doctor Gura as
one of Emperor Bry's
right-hand men, but
behind the scenes, he was
a scheming man who
coveted his superior's
position. He was cunning
and despicable in
character, showing no
discrimination between
friend and foe. In the
past, fearing his position
as marshal was
threatened, he trapped
General Jirai and had him
executed, and when he
predicted that Jirai's son
Jirai Oni would become a
threat, he arranged for
his death in battle as
well. However, he was not
merely a small-time
villain; he possessed
considerable skill, such as
breaking through the
barrier of the new
battleship Sea Force with
his custom fighter, making
a miraculous escape from
an exploding Hyakki Robot,
and even capturing Hayato
as a prisoner during his
escape. But the life he
saved through that
miracle was cut short
when Hayato, his prisoner,
destroyed the Science
Fortress Island from
within, ultimately costing
him his life.

The scientist who serves
as the brains of the
Hyakki Empire, working
alongside Marshal Hidler
as one of Emperor Burai's
right-hand men.
 He is responsible for
developing Hyakki mecha
and fighter craft as well
as drafting strategy, and
his brilliant mind is
indispensable to the
Hyakki Empire.
 Talented young members
such as Jimushiki and
Tekkouki gathered under
him, learning from him day
after day.

Dr. Glah was a scientist
who served as the brain
of the Hyakki Empire.
Alongside Marshal Hidler,
he worked as one of
Emperor Bry's right-hand
men.
 He was responsible for
the development of Hyakki
mecha and fighter craft,
as well as the planning
of operations, and his
superior intellect was
indispensable to the
Hyakki Empire.
 Under his tutelage,
gifted young men such as
Jichki and Tekkouki
gathered and studied
daily.
 He was killed in action
just before the final
battle, but the existence
of the 'Gravity Control
Device' which he left
behind, capable of raising
even the Science Fortress
Island, led Bry to decide
to launch his final
operation.

One of the Hyakki
Hundred, the elite corps
of the Hyakki Empire.
 Supremely confident in
his own intellect, he
developed the Hyakki
mecha Mecha Tekkouki
himself and used it to
challenge Getter Robo.
 His combat ability was
also first-rate, skillful
enough to fight Getter
Robo to a standstill and
beyond. But when Hidler's
tank forced its way into
the battle, his pride was
wounded, and he turned
his blade on Hidler to
protect Getter Robo.
Then, battered and
bloodied, he challenged
Getter to a fair rematch.

Tekkouki was one of the
Hyakki Hundred, the elite
group of the Hyakki
Empire.
 He had absolute
confidence in his own
intellect, and developed
the Hyakki mecha Mecha
Tekkouki to defeat Getter
Robo, challenging it to
battle.
 His combat ability was
also first-rate, showing
skill enough to fight
Getter to a standstill or
better. However, when
Hidler's tank cut in, his
pride was wounded, and he
turned his blade on Hidler
to protect Getter. Then,
while battered and
exhausted, he boldly
challenged Getter to a
rematch. The battle was
decided by Getter
Dragon's Spin Cutter, and
came to a close with
Tekkouki's death.

One of the Hyakki
Hundred, the elite corps
of the Hyakki Empire.
 He had been transforming
dam workers and security
guards into Hyakki
soldiers, and after his
predecessor Ikkakuki fell
to Getter Robo, he took
over the plan to steal
the Getter Ray amplifier.
 Making use of his Hyakki
robot's special traits, he
attempted to attack the
Saotome Institute by
tunneling up from
underground.

Dokuganki was one of
the Hyakki Hundred, the
elite group of the Hyakki
Empire.
 He was converting dam
employees and security
guards into Hyakki
soldiers, but since his
predecessor Ikkakuki had
been defeated by Getter,
he took over and plotted
to seize the Getter Ray
amplifier.
 He attempted to attack
the Saotome Research
Institute from
underground, making use
of his Hyakki robot's
characteristics. However,
while advancing
underground, he was
dragged out by Getter
Liger and killed by four
consecutive missiles.

A veteran warrior among
the Hyakki Hundred, the
elite corps of the Hyakki
Empire.
 Once so formidable that
he was called a hero of
the skies, he had retired
from active duty in his
old age. But when Hidler
lied to him that his son
Gyuugaki had been killed
by Getter Robo, he
resolved to seek revenge.
 Even in old age his skill
had not faded, and his
battle-hardened prowess
put the Getter Team
through real hardship.

Gyukenki was a veteran
of the Hyakki Hundred,
the elite group of the
Hyakki Empire.
 He was a man of such
skill that he was once
called the Hero of the
Sky, but due to old age
he had retired from
active duty. However, due
to Hidler's lie that his
son, Gyugaki, had been
killed by Getter, he
resolved to take revenge.
 Even in his old age, his
skill had not waned, and
with his combat-hardened
experience he troubled
the Getter team. But
when Ryouma pointed out
that 'You, who taught him
nothing but fighting, are
the one who killed your
son,' the shock he
received became the cause
of his defeat.

The pilot of KuRaiOh and
main pilot of God Sigma.
Eighteen years old.
 A man who loved space,
believed in the future,
and fought single-mindedly
for peace. Though he
comes from Io, he speaks
with the brisk,
plainspoken manner of a
true Edokko, a native of
old Tokyo, and he is
warmhearted, spirited, and
hot-blooded, never one to
fuss over small details.
 On Io, he had experience
helping build an ionium
refinery using mining
robots, giving him an edge
when it comes to piloting
machinery. Even KuRaiOh,
which he boarded in an
emergency during an Eldar
attack, he handled as
naturally as his own
limbs.
 He is also a formidable
fighter unarmed, and his
jumping kick in particular
packs a fierce punch.
 Though he and Teral, the
Eldar commander, are
enemies, Toshiya seems to
sense something in him
not unlike himself.

Toshiya Dan was the
main pilot of KuRaiOh and
God Sigma. He was 18
years old.
 He was a man who loved
space, believed in the
future, and fought
wholeheartedly for peace.
Though he was from Io,
he spoke with the brisk
accent of an Edoite, and
was a broad-minded,
spirited, and passionate
man who did not fuss
over details.
 On Io, he had experience
helping build the ionium
refinery using mining
robots, and had an edge
when it came to operating
machines. When the Elder
Army attacked and he was
forced to board KuRaiOh
in an emergency, he
handled it as if it were
an extension of his own
limbs.
 He possessed
considerable combat
ability even in his bare
body, and his kick,
especially when delivered
from a jump, was
ferocious.
 During the war with the
Elders, he came to
sympathize with the
ideals of the enemy
commander Teral, and
eventually they became
friends who called each
other by name.
 In the final battle,
after witnessing Teral's
death as his strength
gave out mid-purpose, he
alone cornered Gagaarn.
Every bullet Gagaarn
sprayed wildly in his last
resistance seemed to be
blocked by an unseen
force, and none struck
Toshiya. But the bullets
Toshiya fired for his
fallen comrades and for
peace pierced Gagaarn for
certain.
 After it was all over,
he departed alone with
God Sigma into the
distant future.

The pilot of KaiMeiOh.
Twenty-one years old.
 An extremely cool-headed
and sharp-tongued man,
whose too-accurate
observations often stir
up trouble. At heart,
though, he is honest and
straightforward - his
foul mouth is simply his
way of covering up an
inability to be candid.
 He also serves as chief
engineer at Trinity Base
and is the
second-sharpest mind
there after Dr. Kazami. A
hard worker, he has made
it his goal to one day
surpass Dr. Kazami
himself.
 His attachment to money
runs strong enough to
seem miserly, though
there appears to be some
deeper reason behind it.

Julie Noguchi is the
pilot of the sea-shaking
king. He is 21 years
old.\nHe is a very cool
and sharp-tongued man,
and his overly accurate
observations often cause
trouble. However, at heart
he is an upright man, and
his harsh words are
simply because he cannot
be honest. At Trinity
Base, he also serves as
chief engineer, possessing
intellect second only to
Dr. Kazami. He is a hard
worker who aims to
surpass Dr. Kazami
someday. His attachment
to money is so strong
that he could be taken
for a miser, but this is
because he is desperately
saving up to go pick up
his mother and younger
sister who are on Io,
revealing his deep
feelings for his family.
After Dr. Kazami was
dazzled by Elder
technology and betrayed
them, he deciphered the
method to release the
lock on the Trinity
Engine, and used the
base's Trinity energy to
successfully combine God
Sigma, so without his
intellect the Earth side's
victory would not have
been possible. After the
battle with Gagarn ended,
he saw off Toshiya who
was departing with the
words of encouragement
'Leave Io to me.'

The pilot of RikuShinOh.
 He lost both parents
before his own eyes in an
Eldar attack, yet his
bright, straightforward
personality shows none of
that tragedy. That said,
he is also a flatterer, a
show-off, and something
of a daredevil. Perhaps
because they are close in
maturity, he gets along
especially well with Rie's
younger brother Shouta,
who looks up to him like
an older brother.
 Hopeless with machines
by nature, he could not
even handle RikuShinOh
well at first. But when
he learned that God Sigma
could be formed and that
KuRaiOh would be its main
unit, he pushed Toshiya
aside and climbed into
KuRaiOh himself. KuRaiOh's
onboard computer,
however, declared as a
piloting requirement,
"Fighting spirit alone is
not enough. A calm mind
and trained skill are
required," making him
painfully aware of what
he lacked. From then on,
through sheer grit, he
gradually managed to get
the hang of at least
RikuShinOh.

Kensaku Kira is the
pilot of the land-shaking
king. He lost both
parents before his eyes
to the Elder attack, but
he has a bright and
straightforward
personality that does not
show that tragedy.
However, he is a bit of a
fool, a show-off, and
also has a reckless side.
Perhaps because their
mental ages are close, he
gets along especially well
with Rie's younger
brother Shota, and is
looked up to as a big
brother figure. He is a
natural klutz with
machines, and at first
could not even pilot the
land-shaking king well.
But when he learned that
combining into God Sigma
was possible, and that
the sky-shaking king
would be the core unit,
he climbed into the
sky-shaking king, pushing
Toshiya aside. However,
the sky-shaking king's
internal computer declared
as a piloting condition:
'Fighting spirit alone is
not enough. You need a
cool head and trained
skills.' He keenly felt his
own shortcomings. After
that, with his
characteristic
determination, he managed
to at least handle the
land-shaking king. When
the battle with the Elder
ended and Toshiya was
about to depart for the
future, he sent him off
with the affectionate
words 'Be sure to come
back.'

Dr. Kazami's
stepdaughter and
secretary.
 An exceptionally gifted
young woman, she
skillfully supported Dr.
Kazami to keep Trinity
Base's wide-ranging
operations running
smoothly.
 She had been living
apart from her younger
brother Shouta, but the
two later came to live
together inside the base.
 She secretly harbors
feelings for Toshiya, and
keeps a photograph of him
displayed in her room.
 In place of Dr. Kazami,
who opposed sending
Trinity Base to Jupiter
until the very end, she
came to take full
command of the base
after its departure.

Rie Kasuga is Dr.
Kazami's secretary and
also his stepdaughter. She
is a highly capable and
talented woman, skillfully
supporting Dr. Kazami so
that the many varied
duties of Trinity Base do
not fall behind. She lived
apart from her younger
brother Shota, but later
they came to live
together in the base. She
harbors feelings for
Toshiya, and a photo of
him is displayed in her
room. She took over
command of the entire
base after departure, in
place of Dr. Kazami who
had opposed the base
moving to Jupiter until
the very end. She
overcame the betrayal of
the doctor she respected,
fought through against
the Elder army, and
finally saved the Earth.
Although her beloved
Toshiya departed for the
future, no shadow of
gloom could be seen on
her face as she watched
him leave.

Martino's daughter.
 As her high-fashion
sense suggests, she is
overconfident and willful,
the type to do whatever
she pleases.
 She calls herself
Toshiya's girlfriend and is
a rival to Rie.
 She is also a
troublemaker, repeatedly
acting on her own
impulses in ways that
both create and resolve
crises for God Sigma.

Martino's daughter.
 As her high-fashion
sense suggests, she is
overconfident and willful,
the type to do whatever
she pleases.
 She calls herself
Toshiya's girlfriend and is
a rival to Rie.
 She is also a
troublemaker, repeatedly
acting on her own
impulses in ways that
both create and resolve
crises for God Sigma.

The financial backer of
Trinity City.
 A self-centered man
obsessed with money, who
judges every action solely
by whether it will turn a
profit. This is plain
enough from the fact
that, even in the midst
of the Eldar invasion, he
tried to sell off KuRaiOh,
KaiMeiOh, and RikuShinOh.
 Yet his love for his
daughter Minako runs
deep, and he treasures
her just as much as his
money.

The financial backer of
Trinity City.
 A self-centered man
obsessed with money, who
judges every action solely
by whether it will turn a
profit. This is plain
enough from the fact
that, even in the midst
of the Elder invasion, he
tried to sell off KuRaiOh,
KaiMeiOh, and RikuShinOh.
 Yet his love for his
daughter Minako runs
deep, and he treasures
her just as much as his
money.

The genius scientist who
developed both Trinity
Energy, said to be phase
energy extracted from a
distortion in dimensional
space, and God Sigma
itself.
 Gentle and tolerant by
nature, he took in the
orphaned Rie and treats
Toshiya and the others
with the same warmth as
a parent. His keen mind
also makes him a capable
battle commander, and he
serves as the spiritual
pillar of Trinity Base.

Dr. Kazami is the genius
scientist who developed
Trinity energy - said to
be phase energy taken
from a dimensional rift -
and God Sigma. He is
mild-mannered and
tolerant, taking in Rie
who was an orphan, and
treating Toshiya and the
others warmly like family.
His battle command using
his intellect is also
sound, and he is the
spiritual pillar of Trinity
Base. But behind that, he
was captivated by Elder
super-science, and had a
side as a mad scientist
who would capture Elder
aliens and torture them
to extract their secrets.
This came to the surface
during the torture of
Teral, and afterwards he
gradually began to clash
with Toshiya and the
others. When Trinity Base
fell into crisis, he
unilaterally declared
defeat, sealed the Trinity
Engine, and ran off alone
to Gagarn. Then, to seize
Trinity Base as the
condition offered for
boarding the time ship, he
turned his fangs on his
former comrades. His end
came when he pointed a
gun at Julie who was
trying to release the
Trinity Engine seal, and
was shot in the back by
an Elder soldier. The
keyword to release the
seal was 'I am the genius
and the world's greatest
mind! I am the genius and
the world's greatest
mind!' - filled with Dr.
Kazami's impatience with
super-science and his
pride as a scientist.

The supreme commander
leading the Eldar forces.
 He was dispatched to
Earth's past under orders
from the Eldar Council to
seize Trinity Energy.
 He commands the
absolute trust of his two
lieutenants and his many
subordinates, seeking to
accomplish his mission
through unity. However,
he runs into unexpectedly
fierce resistance from
God Sigma, throwing his
plans badly off course.
 When sending out two of
his subordinates who are
lovers, he gives them
especially strong
encouragement and even
looks after them
afterward, and he is
visibly moved by the way
his enemies Toshiya and
Rie disregard their own
safety for each other's
sake. He has a soft spot
for men and women who
care for one another,
revealing at times a
somewhat feminine side.

Teral is the supreme
commander leading the
Elder army. He was
dispatched to Earth in
the past on orders from
the Elder homeworld's
senate to seize Trinity
energy. He is trusted
enormously by his two
adjutants and many
subordinates, and strives
to accomplish his goals
through unity. However,
he encounters
unexpectedly fierce
resistance from God
Sigma, throwing his plans
into great disarray. When
sending out his two
subordinates who are
lovers, he encourages
them with particular vigor
and even tries to look
after them afterwards,
and he is disturbed by
the actions of enemies
Toshiya and Rie who
disregard their own
safety for each other -
he is weak to men and
women who care for one
another, and sometimes
shows a somewhat
feminine side. This was
largely due to a secret
hidden in Teral's heart
and body. Later, he is
stripped of his commander
position by Gagarn, who
was sent by the senate
when their patience ran
out. He is driven to the
brink of execution, but
escapes with the help of
his subordinates and
reaches Earth. There, he
and his former enemies
Toshiya and the others
come to understand each
other and join hands.
After the reconciliation,
he acts alone, eliminating
Gagarn's adjutants Dalton
and Mesa, and finally
closes in on Gagarn
himself. But his strength
is insufficient, and he is
struck down. He entrusts
the future of the Elder
race to Toshiya who
rushes to his side, and
his soul departs on a
journey to his lover.

The woman whose spirit
now resides within Teral.
 Originally Teral's lover,
she was aboard a
battleship struck by an
attack from Earth's
forces in the future;
Teral shielded her from
the blast, but he was
buried beneath the falling
debris and died.
 Vowing both revenge
against the Earth that
had torn them apart and
to spend her whole life
together with her beloved
Teral, she used a special
procedure to fuse her
own spirit with Teral's
body.

The woman whose spirit
now resides within Teral.
 Originally Teral's lover,
she was aboard a
battleship struck by an
attack from Earth's
forces in the future;
Teral shielded her from
the blast, but he was
buried beneath the falling
debris and died.
 Vowing both revenge
against the Earth that
had torn them apart and
to spend her whole life
together with her beloved
Teral, she used a special
procedure to fuse her
own spirit with Teral's
body.

An Eldar military
commander under Teral,
responsible for developing
the Cosmosaurus.
 He is devoted to Teral,
and his efforts to seize
Trinity Energy seem
driven less by loyalty to
his homeland than by
devotion to Teral himself.
 He and his colleague
Ritsu are on famously bad
terms, but he has the
flexibility to work with
him willingly whenever it
is for Teral's sake.

Jira was a commander of
the Elder military under
Terral, and was in charge
of developing the
Cosmosaurus. He was
devoted to Terral, and
his desire to obtain
Trinity Energy felt more
like it was for Terral's
sake than for his
homeland. He had a bitter
relationship with his
colleague Lietz, but he
possessed the flexibility
to willingly cooperate if
it was for Terral's sake.
After the appearance of
Gagarn, who opposed
Terral, he went so far as
to cooperate with him
throughout. When Gagarn
seized full authority over
the Earth attack and
moved to execute Terral,
Jira acted quickly and
volunteered for the role
of executioner,
successfully placing
Terral in a state of
suspended animation to
help him escape. He
seemed to have driven off
the pursuers sent by
Gagarn, who had learned
the full truth, in a
gunfight, but he was
struck in the back by a
bullet from a pursuer who
was still alive. At the
brink of death, Terral
regained consciousness
and accused him of
treachery, but Jira
deliberately did not deny
it. Then, smiling
contentedly that Terral
was safe, he fell into an
eternal sleep. Seeing this,
Terral realized the depth
of Jira's loyalty and shed
tears.

An Eldar military
commander under Teral.
 A fierce warrior, he
clashes with God Sigma
again and again in pursuit
of Trinity Energy for the
sake of his homeland and
Teral. Yet he is in
constant conflict with
Jira, who develops the
Cosmosaurus so vital to
their operations. Even so,
when Teral is in danger,
the two set aside their
usual bickering and work
together in perfect sync.
 He serves Teral with
unwavering loyalty as his
subject, and has even
risked his own life to
save him from danger.

Lietz was a commander
of the Elder military
under Terral. A brave
warrior, he clashed with
God Sigma many times in
order to seize Trinity
Energy for the sake of
his homeland and Terral.
However, he had an
unending feud with Jira,
who developed the
Cosmosaurus essential to
their operations. Even so,
when Terral faced a
crisis, they showed a
surprising unity quite
unlike their usual
behavior. He served Terral
with the loyalty of a
retainer, and had even
risked his life to save
him from danger. When
Gagarn seized full
authority over the Earth
attack and insulted
Terral, Lietz reached his
limit and cut off the
head of the Lot Bird that
had been set upon him.
Turning his blade on
Gagarn, he was blocked by
Mesa's gunfire. Though his
body was riddled with
holes, he pressed on to
within a step of his goal
before his strength gave
out, and he collapsed
while speaking words
praising Terral. His
stubbornly earnest end
brought tears not only to
Terral's eyes, but also to
those of Jira, his rival.

A soldier who came from
the Eldar homeworld
ostensibly to assist
Teral.
 Extremely cunning and
ruthless, he will use any
means necessary to
achieve his ends. He did
not come to the present
era to save his homeworld
Eldar, but rather to seize
Trinity Energy, depose
the Eldar Council, and
rule Eldar himself.
 To that end, Teral's
presence is an obstacle,
and Gagarn has employed
various schemes to
undermine him. He once
stormed Teral's base,
forcing a situation where
Teral had no choice but
to fight back, then
destroyed the base and
claimed it had been
"self-defense." Within the
base as well, he ruled
Teral's soldiers with an
iron fist, and eventually
ousted Teral to take the
position of supreme
commander of the invasion
of Earth.
 He is no mere villain,
however; his abilities
are considerable. Leading
a fleet into battle or
piloting the giant robot
Gargos, he overwhelmed
God Sigma from start to
finish. He also possesses
a sharp eye for
observation, having seen
through Teral's true
nature even when Teral's
own direct subordinates
Ritsu and Jira had not.
 He keeps as a pet a
Lotbird, a creature both
strikingly colorful and
formidable in combat.

Gagarn was a military
man who came from the
Elder homeworld under the
pretext of assisting
Terral. Extremely cunning
and cruel by nature, he
would stop at nothing to
achieve his goals. His
arrival in the present
was not to save his
homeland of Elder, but to
obtain Trinity Energy,
supplant the Senate, and
seize control of Elder for
himself. To that end,
Terral's existence was an
obstacle, and he employed
various means to
undermine his power. On
one occasion, he attacked
Terral's base, created a
situation where they had
no choice but to fight
back, and then destroyed
the base while claiming it
was 'self-defense.' At
the base, he also used
force to dominate
Terral's soldiers, and
eventually ousted Terral
to take the position of
Supreme Commander of the
Earth attack. However, he
was not merely a villain;
his abilities were
extremely high. In fleet
battles leading his
forces, and in combat
piloting the giant robot
Gargos, he consistently
overwhelmed God Sigma. He
also possessed sharp
observational skills,
seeing through Terral's
true identity, which even
his direct subordinates
Lietz and Jira had failed
to notice. In the final
battle within the
fortress, seeing the tide
turn against him, he
attempted to escape alone
to the future via a Time
Ship, but Terral gave
chase and halted him. In
a gunfight, he took
Terral's life and tried to
flee again, but was
cornered by Toshiya. In
the end, he was shot
through the chest,
abdomen, and forehead and
died.

Gagarn's lieutenant and
combat commander.
 With his red skin, harsh
scowl, powerful build, and
overbearing manner, he
cuts an intimidating
figure. His true
character, though, is far
less impressive:
extremely bold whenever
he has the upper hand,
but instantly reduced to
cowardice the moment
things turn against him.

Dalton was Gagarn's
adjutant and combat
commander. His red skin,
stern expression, robust
physique, and overbearing
attitude gave him an
imposing appearance.
However, his true
character was pathetic:
he was extremely bold
when he held the
advantage, but instantly
turned timid the moment
he fell even slightly into
a disadvantage. In the
battle of Io, when his
ship was destroyed and
he was discovered by
Terral while escaping, he
fell to his knees and
begged for his life. When
Taichirou intervened
against Terral, who
declared 'End your life
honorably,' Dalton seized
the opening and opened
fire, wounding Taichirou.
In the end, as he fled
with his back turned, he
received Terral's furious
strike and vanished into
the abyss.

Gagarn's lieutenant and
chief of science.
 He creates new models
of the Cosmosaurus and
devises operations that
make use of them.
 His brilliant mind earns
him recognition even from
Gagarn, who relies on him
as a right-hand man. Yet
he seems to regard
betrayal as a virtue,
having switched his
allegiance to Teral not
once but twice.

Mesa was Gagarn's
adjutant and science
chief. He created new
types of Cosmosaurus and
devised operations using
them. Gagarn valued his
excellent intellect and
relied heavily on him as a
right-hand man. However,
he seemed to consider
betrayal a virtue, having
bowed his head to Terral
on two occasions. The
first time, his sincere
attitude convinced even
Terral, but once his
personal safety was
assured, he immediately
betrayed him. The second
time, he attempted to
shoot Terral in the back
after he had infiltrated
Gagarn's fortress, but
failed, and begged for his
life. Given the previous
incident, Terral would not
accept. But when allied
soldiers' covering fire
caused Terral to lose his
gun, Mesa promptly
switched to an
overbearing manner and
aimed his weapon to
finish him off. At that
moment, a sudden shock
ran through the fortress,
and Terral seized a gun
from a soldier in the
confusion. Terral and
Mesa fired simultaneously,
but only Mesa was struck
through the skull and
died.

Julie's younger sister.
 A spirited girl, she
fought alongside the men
as a member of the Cosmo
Factory. After being
wounded, she happened
upon Teral, who was
fleeing Gagarn's pursuers,
and tended to his
injuries. Learning that
even among the Eldar -
whom she had only ever
hated - there were those
capable of kindness, she
reconsidered her
one-sided view of them.
 Afterward, she saved
Teral's life twice over:
once from the Factory
members who insisted he
should be executed, and
once from the gunfire of
the pursuing Eldar
soldiers.

Jane Nishino was Julie's
younger sister. She was a
headstrong girl who, as a
member of the Cosmo
Factory, participated in
combat alongside the men.
While wounded, she
happened upon Terral, who
was fleeing from Gagarn's
pursuers, and received
treatment for her injuries
from him. Through this
encounter, she learned
that even among the
Elders, whom she had only
ever seen as objects of
hatred, there were those
who possessed kindness,
and she revised her
one-sided views.
Afterwards, she saved
Terral's life twice: once
from the Factory members
who insisted he should be
executed, and once from
the gunfire of the Elder
army soldiers pursuing
him. She set out for
Earth aboard a spaceship
together with Terral
after he disposed of the
pursuers, but they were
assailed by Gagarn's
pursuit. With the aid of
God Sigma, they barely
managed to reach Earth,
but she was already in a
dying state due to the
bullet wounds from the
earlier attack and the
shock of the spaceship's
explosion. Telling Julie,
who rushed to her side,
that 'Terral is a good
person,' she breathed her
last in her brother's
arms.

Toshiya's father.
 As chairman of the
Cosmo Factory, he served
as the leader of Io's
inhabitants. After
escaping the Eldar's
attack, he has led the
surviving residents in a
life on the run.
 He is a man who makes
calm decisions without
being swept up by emotion
or circumstance. When the
Factory members, driven
by anger, demanded that
Teral - then being
pursued by Gagarn - be
executed, Taichiro instead
decided he should be
handed over as a prisoner
to Dr. Kazami, and won
the others over to his
view.

Dan Taichirou was
Toshiya's father. As the
chairman of the Cosmo
Factory, he served as the
leader who rallied the
people living on Io. After
escaping the Elders'
attack, he led the
surviving residents in a
life of flight. He was a
man capable of calm
judgment, unswayed by
emotion or circumstance.
Regarding the treatment
of Terral, who was being
pursued by Gagarn, when
the Factory members
angrily demanded his
execution, Taichirou
decided instead that
Terral should be delivered
as a prisoner to Dr.
Kazami and persuaded the
others to accept this.
Later, cooperating with
the Terral he had
reunited with, he
distinguished himself by
repelling Gagarn's attacks
until Toshiya and the
others arrived at Io. He
also at last met face to
face with Toshiya, but
collapsed due to wounds
suffered during the
fighting. From his sickbed,
he delivered a final
rallying cry to Toshiya
as he engaged in a deadly
struggle with Gargos, and
then closed his eyes,
bringing his life to an
end.

A young man belonging
to the Free Space Force.
Nineteen years old.
 In the year 2062, before
the world descended into
spacetime chaos, he and
Orson were partners both
on and off duty.
 Dispatched on a mission
to destroy an orbital
elevator occupied by
hostile forces, Kei fought
to protect the spacetime
vibration bomb at the
heart of the operation,
but the enemy's fierce
assault forced a retreat.
Along the retreat route,
he discovered an
unadjusted spacetime
vibration bomb, and in a
bid to strike back at the
enemy, he activated it.
 Caught up in the
spacetime chaos this
unleashed, the world
plunged into the Chaos
Century, dragging parallel
universes into the
upheaval along with it.
Kei became an Anomaly
and was cast twenty
years into the future.

A young man belonging
to the Free Space Force.
Nineteen years old.
 In the year 2062, before
the world descended into
spacetime chaos, he and
Orson were partners both
on and off duty.
 Dispatched on a mission
to destroy an orbital
elevator occupied by
hostile forces, Kei fought
to protect the spacetime
vibration bomb at the
heart of the operation,
but the enemy's fierce
assault forced a retreat.
Along the retreat route,
he discovered an
unadjusted spacetime
vibration bomb, and in a
bid to strike back at the
enemy, he activated it.
 Caught up in the
spacetime chaos this
unleashed, the world
plunged into the Chaos
Century, dragging parallel
universes into the
upheaval along with it.
Kei became an Anomaly
and was cast twenty
years into the future.

A young man of nineteen
who came to be known as
the Anomaly in a world
sealed within the Realm
of Conflict.
 He seems at first glance
a typical hot-blooded,
straightforward hero
type, but underneath he
is easygoing to a fault
and an incorrigible
womanizer. Even in the
world before the
spacetime chaos, he
carried on relationships
with countless women, and
with one girlfriend in
particular, Tina, he kept
up secret trysts between
military duties.
 After being transported
to the world twenty
years later, he was
rescued by the Emaan
caravan of the Factory
led by Shaya, who told
him he was the Anomaly.
Learning that he himself
was the cause of the
world's turmoil, and that
his existence was needed
to repair it, he resolved
to travel with the
Factory.
 While mainly courting
Mimsy, he also made
passes at other women he
spotted along the way,
repeatedly stirring up
trouble.
 He possesses a natural
talent for piloting: the
inertial control system,
an unfamiliar technology
to him, he mastered after
only a brief explanation
and a little practice.
Piloting the Molaba and
the Orguss, he repeatedly
drove back the Chiram
army as it pursued Glomar
in an attempt to seize
the Anomaly.

Kei Katsuragi was a
young man who came to
be called the Anomaly in
the world sealed within
the dimension of mutual
interference. He was 19
years old. One might have
taken him for the typical
hero type - impetuous
and hot-blooded - but in
truth he had a frivolous
nature and was an
incurable womanizer. Even
in the world before the
space-time disruption, he
had been involved with
countless women, and
among them, with Tina,
one of his lovers, he had
stolen moments of
rendezvous between
military duties. After
being transferred to the
world twenty years later,
he was rescued by the
Emaan Factory caravan led
by Shaya and was told
that he was the Anomaly.
Learning that he was the
cause of the world's
disruption and that his
existence was needed to
repair it, he resolved to
accompany the Factory.
While primarily wooing
Mimsy, he would also make
passes at any woman he
encountered along the
way, frequently stirring
up trouble. He possessed
an innate piloting talent,
mastering the Inertial
Control System - a
technology entirely
unknown to him - after
only a brief explanation
and a little practice. He
drove the Morabaa and
Orguss to repel one after
another the Chiram forces
that sought to seize the
Anomaly from Glomar.
Eventually, he encountered
Orson, who had also
become an Anomaly, and
Athena, the daughter born
to him and Tina. Initially
they were hostile due to
their respective
circumstances, but
gradually they came to
join hands and deepen
their bonds. In the end,
together with Orson, he
plunged into the Great
Anomaly, which had
originally been a
space-time vibration bomb,
and within it encountered
their past selves. This
space-time disruption had
occurred because another
persona of Kei and of
Orson had existed in the
same time. To restore the
space-time disruption, the
two pulled the triggers
aimed at their own past
selves. In the infinite
possibilities of the
future shown in the
epilogue, a vision of him
holding a child he had
fathered with Mimsy could
also be seen.

An Emaan woman who
serves as chief of the
Factory.
 Studious and thoughtful
by nature, but also
worldly-naive and far too
much on her own
wavelength.
 Emaan women have a
fertile period, after
which they lose their
reproductive function.
However, their bodies
undergo almost no further
change afterward, so even
though she is already
nearing thirty, Shaya still
retains a youthful
appearance. Emaan people
also lose their sense of
sexual modesty once their
fertile period ends, so
they think nothing of
exposing themselves. Even
a seasoned playboy like
Kei was left stunned when
she calmly walked into
the bath while he was
using it.
 Though born into the
prestigious Tobu family,
she left politics to her
twin sister and continued
her carefree life with
the caravan - until she
encountered Kei. Learning
that he was the Anomaly
needed to repair the
spacetime chaos, she
decided to protect him.
This choice, however, put
her at odds not only with
Chiram but with her own
sister Manisha, a fact
that weighs heavily on
her.

Shaya Tob was an Emaan
woman serving as the
chief of the Factory. She
was scholarly and
thoughtful, but also naive
about the world and far
too inclined to go at her
own pace. Emaan women
have a reproductive
period, and once this
period passes, they lose
their reproductive
function. However, since
their physical changes
also almost cease
thereafter, despite
already being nearly
thirty years old, she
still retained a youthful
appearance. Furthermore,
because Emaan women lose
their sexual modesty once
their reproductive period
ends, they no longer care
about exposing their
bodies. When she casually
entered the bath while
Kei was using it, even
that playboy was
thoroughly taken aback.
Although she came from
the distinguished Tob
family, she had left
politics to her twin
sister and was living
freely with the caravan
when she encountered Kei.
Learning that Kei was the
Anomaly needed to repair
the disrupted space-time,
she decided to protect
him. However, this choice
pained her, as it brought
her into conflict not only
with Chiram but also with
her own younger sister,
Manisha. Later, however,
she succeeded in
reconciling with her
sister, and formed an
alliance with Chiram as
well for the common
purpose of repairing
space-time. In the
infinite possibilities seen
after Kei and the others
plunged into the Great
Anomaly, there was a
vision of her nestled
beside Ranchi, a former
lover who had once
stepped aside for her
sister's sake.

An Emaan girl of
seventeen, born in the
Chaos Century.
 She comes from the Raas
family, a prominent house
among the Emaan, and is
its heir.
 She met Kei while
gaining experience with
the caravan as a member
of the Factory. She
already had a fiance in
the Factory, Slay, but
found herself drawn to
the forward Kei, and her
heart wavered.
 Like other Emaan, Mimsy
apparently has a twin
sister as well, but she is
said to lack an active
personality and did not
join the caravan.

Mimsy Lass was an Emaan
girl born in the century
of disrupted space-time.
She was 17 years old. She
came from the Lass
family, a distinguished
house among the Emaan,
and was its heiress. While
gaining caravan experience
as a member of the
Factory, she met Kei. She
already had a fiance,
Slay, in the Factory, but
she was drawn to the
assertive Kei and her
heart began to waver. As
the end of her
reproductive period
approached, she was
stricken by nightmares
and collapsed. Driven by
that anxiety, she
confronted her own
feelings honestly and at
one point promised to
marry Slay. But
immediately afterwards,
she came under attack
from Manisha's pursuit
forces seeking to seize
Kei, and Slay, who had
sortied for Mimsy's sake,
lost his life. She was
plunged into deep grief
for a time, but eventually
recovered and came to
share her heart with Kei,
ultimately conceiving a
child with him. Like other
Emaan women, Mimsy
apparently also had a
twin sister, but that
sister seems not to have
been of an active
disposition and did not
participate in the
caravan.

A humanoid built on Mu.
Her appearance is
indistinguishable from a
human girl's.
 Swept up in a spacetime
transfer and carried to
Atlantis, she was put up
for sale there. Kei
bought her, and she
became a member of
Glomar.
 Designed to become
friends with humans, she
possesses emotional
circuits equivalent to a
human's. As a result, she
gradually came to fall in
love with Kei, who was
also her benefactor.
 Having been built for
nursing and repair work,
she handled a wide range
of tasks, from everyday
chores to mechanical
maintenance.

Mome was a humanoid
built on Mu,
indistinguishable in
appearance from a human
girl. After being caught
in a spacetime shift and
transported to Atlantis,
she was put up for sale
as merchandise. Kei
bought her there, and she
became a member of the
Glomar crew. She was
designed to befriend
humans, and thus
possessed emotional
circuits equivalent to
those of a human.
Because of this, she
gradually came to harbor
feelings of love for Kei,
her benefactor. Built for
nursing and repair duties,
she was capable of
handling a wide range of
tasks, from daily chores
to mechanical maintenance.
During the final battle
against Mu, she channeled
her own energy into the
Daimora's main cannon to
repel the enemy and save
Mimsy. However, by the
time Kei rushed to her
side, she had already
exhausted all her energy,
and closed her eyes in
his arms. Soon after, bid
farewell by Kei's tears,
she vanished into the
depths of space.

Lieea's twin older
sister.
 A spirited girl who
bravely confronts the
enemy in her Molaba
whenever battle breaks
out.
 Because Emaan have a
limited reproductive
period, they are normally
born as twins. However,
as far as anyone has
observed, these two
sisters are practically
the only twin pair who
act together, which makes
them a rare and valuable
pair in more ways than
one.

Lieea's twin older
sister.
 A spirited girl who
bravely confronts the
enemy in her Molaba
whenever battle breaks
out.
 Because Emaan have a
limited reproductive
period, they are normally
born as twins. However,
as far as anyone has
observed, these two
sisters are practically
the only twin pair who
act together, which makes
them a rare and valuable
pair in more ways than
one.

Maaie's twin younger
sister.
 She is every bit as
much of a tomboy as her
sister. She sometimes
bristles with rivalry at
Maaie's older-sister airs,
but the two generally get
along well.
 She has the nerve to
climb into her own Molaba
and fight aerial battles,
but since she is not a
soldier, she hesitates to
harm a person directly.

Maaie's twin younger
sister.
 She is every bit as
much of a tomboy as her
sister. She sometimes
bristles with rivalry at
Maaie's older-sister airs,
but the two generally get
along well.
 She has the nerve to
climb into her own Molaba
and fight aerial battles,
but since she is not a
soldier, she hesitates to
harm a person directly.

A member of a
parallel-universe branch
of humanity with a
dinosaur-like appearance.
 He is searching for a
lover from whom he was
separated during a
spacetime transfer.
 With a burner built into
his mouth, he repeatedly
breathed fire to drive
off attacking Mozuku
raiders, and during
trading runs he instead
put that same
fire-breathing to use
drawing in customers. He
also proved useful in
other ways, such as when
he used his keen sense
of smell to locate a
vineyard after Glomar ran
out of trade goods. He is
also the one who named
the Orguss.
 He remembers the
sensation of the
spacetime transfer he
once experienced, and can
sense its warning signs
through his tail's
reactions, which has more
than once let Glomar
avoid disaster.

Jabby was a type of
Earthling from a parallel
universe with a
dinosaur-like appearance.
He was searching for his
lover, from whom he had
been separated when both
were caught in a
spacetime shift. He had a
burner built into his
mouth, and used it to
drive off the Mozuku
tribe, who frequently
attacked by spitting fire,
while on trading trips he
would instead use it to
attract customers. When
the Glomar's trade goods
were lost, his keen sense
of smell once led him to
discover a vineyard,
making him a useful
presence in many ways. He
was also the one who
named the Orguss. He
remembered the sensation
of the spacetime shifts
he had experienced in the
past, and could sense
their approach through a
reaction in his tail, which
allowed the Glomar to
escape danger on several
occasions. As their
journey continued, he
finally found his homeland
as he had wished.
However, it had been
reduced to ruins, with
not only the lover he had
been seeking but even his
comrades all dead.
Overwhelmed by despair at
the devastation, he
wished to stay behind
alone and die. Yet,
persuaded by Kei, he
changed his mind and
returned to the Glomar,
which had become his
second home.

An engineer with the
Factory.
 When Kei's Bronco II was
wrecked, Reeg used his
own technical skill to
repair and modify it,
building the Orguss.

League was a technician
at the Factory. When the
Bronco II that Kei had
been riding was
destroyed, League used
his considerable technical
skill to repair and modify
it, creating the Orguss.
After the alliance with
Chiram, he worked
together with Chiram's
technicians to complete
the spacetime conversion
device.

An Emaan man and
member of the Factory.
 Physically weak and
slight of build, he gives
an androgynous impression.
He is Mimsy's fiance, and
hopes to be joined with
her before her fertile
second period of
development - during
which she is able to bear
children - comes to an
end, but he has struggled
since she will not accept
him.
 When Kei suddenly
appeared and began
pursuing Mimsy, Slay
turned his hostility on
him, at one point even
pressing Shaya to drive
Kei out.
 His feelings for Mimsy
are genuine: when she
was nearly carried off by
a Mozuku warrior, he
picked an obviously
unwinnable fight to
protect her.

Slay was an Emaan man
and a member of the
Factory. Weak and slender
of build, he gave an
androgynous impression. He
was Mimsy's fiance, and
wished to be united with
her before her secondary
sexual characteristics,
which would allow her to
bear children, came to an
end, but she would not
accept him, and he was
at his wit's end. Then
Kei suddenly appeared and
began courting Mimsy, so
Slay directed his hostility
at Kei, once even working
through Shaya to have
him expelled. His feelings
for Mimsy were genuine;
when she was nearly
carried off by a Mozuku
warrior, he picked a fight
he was clearly outmatched
in to protect her. He
left the caravan for a
time, but returned to the
Glomar just as Mimsy's
reproductive window was
about to close. He
promised marriage to
Mimsy, who called his
name in her delirium, and
shook hands with Kei as
well. Just as it seemed
everything would be
settled peacefully, they
were struck by Manisha's
pursuit force. He sortied
in the Orguss II to
protect Mimsy, but was
soon hit. Then, resolved,
he rammed his craft into
the enemy ship and fell
in battle, never having
been united with Mimsy.

An old man who travels
with the Factory.
 A born merchant, he
thinks nothing of shady
dealings, such as passing
off scraps of battle
mecha as precious gems
to sell to unsuspecting
Atlantans.
 He and Kei seemed to
get along well, sharing
drinks together and
playing a game similar to
Othello.

Gove was an old man who
accompanied the Factory.
He was a true merchant
of the stripe who would
unblinkingly engage in
shady dealings, such as
palming off scraps of
combat mecha to ignorant
Atlantans as precious
gems. He seemed to get
along well with Kei,
drinking with him and
playing a game similar to
Othello. When Mimsy
became pregnant, he again
proposed the name 'Gamon'
for the child, the same
name he had suggested
when the Orguss was
being named. Why he was
so attached to that name
was unknown.

An Emaan woman and
member of the Factory.
 Her husband was killed
by Chiram soldiers, and
she now raises her
surviving twin babies, Vee
and Rom, as her sole
reason for living.
 She helps out with a
variety of tasks aboard
Glomar, from mechanical
maintenance to manning
the machine guns.

An Emaan woman and
member of the Factory.
 Her husband was killed
by Chiram soldiers, and
she now raises her
surviving twin babies, Vee
and Rom, as her sole
reason for living.
 She helps out with a
variety of tasks aboard
Glomar, from mechanical
maintenance to manning
the machine guns.

A robot warrior built on
Mu two hundred years
ago, designed for
close-quarters combat and
mid- to short-range
ground warfare. His rank
is, fittingly, Captain.
 He was a combat
commander attached to
the 11th Combat Squadron
of the 22nd Battalion,
Eslina Area Army, but was
caught in a spacetime
transfer during battle
and thrown into the
European region, where he
shut down.
 When Glomar fled into
Europe to escape Chiram,
Kei and Mome, scavenging
for salvageable junk,
found and repaired him,
and he became a member
of Glomar.
 His excessive pride
often got in the way of
swift action, and he was
reluctant to use Emaan
weapons, which more than
once left him out of step
with those around him.
But once he is truly
committed, his combat
ability is a sight to
behold.

Born in Mu 200 years
ago, this robot warrior
was designed for infantry
combat and
close-to-mid-range ground
warfare. Its rank,
needless to say, is
Captain. It served as a
combat commander in the
11th Combat Platoon of
the 22nd Battalion of the
Esrina Front Army, but
during battle it was
caught up in a space-time
shift and thrown to the
Europe region, where its
activity ceased. When
Gargos fled to Europe to
escape Chiram, it was
found by Kei and Mome,
who were searching for
reusable junk, and was
repaired, becoming a
member of the Gargos
crew. Its excessive pride
often hindered rapid
action, and it disliked
using Emaan weapons,
frequently failing to stay
in step with those around
it. However, once it
became serious, its
combat ability was
remarkable. When Kei and
the others made their
push into the Great
Anomaly, it exposed itself
to gunfire to hold back
Mu's fierce assault. It
seemed to have followed
after Mome, but it barely
survived, and went on to
face an even stranger
fate. That, however, is
an episode that should be
told in another story.

Kei's girlfriend in the
world before the
spacetime chaos.
 Her father never
approved of her
relationship with Kei, so
the two carried on secret
trysts, during which she
conceived Kei's child,
Athena.
 The world soon plunged
into the Chaos Century.
She gave birth while Kei
was missing, and raised
their daughter alone,
without a father present,
ever after.
 In the eighteenth year
of the Chaos Century, she
was caught in a Mu
attack and died without
ever being reunited with
Kei.

The daughter of Kei and
Tina, born on February 20
of the second year of
the Chaos Century.
Eighteen years old.
 She enlisted as a child
soldier in the Chiram army
from the age of eleven
and worked as a soldier
from then on. She met
Orson when he was placed
under the protection of
her grandfather Michael,
and came to see in him
her image of an ideal
father.
 When her mother and
grandfather were later
killed in a Mu attack, she
resolved to fight not for
revenge, but so that no
one else would have to
suffer the same grief she
had. She volunteered for
a transfer to the front
line, where Orson drilled
her in combat technique.
The result was a
first-rate woman warrior,
combining a woman's
delicacy with the
bloodline of a gifted
pilot.
 Toward the father she
has never even seen, she
harbors both the
loneliness of his absence
and resentment for the
hardship he caused her
mother and grandfather.

Born on February 20 of
Year 2 of the Chaotic
Time-Space Century, she
is the daughter of Kei
and Tina. She is 18 years
old. From the age of 11
she enlisted as a child
soldier in the Chiram
military and worked as a
soldier. She met Orson
when he was placed under
the protection of her
grandfather Michael, and
she saw in him the ideal
image of a father. When
her mother and
grandfather were later
killed in a Mu attack, she
resolved to fight not for
revenge, but so that no
more people would have to
taste the same sorrow
she had known. She
volunteered for a
transfer to the front
lines and was drilled in
combat techniques by
Orson. As a result, the
delicacy of a woman
combined with the
bloodline of a genius
pilot gave birth to a
first-rate female warrior.
Towards her father, whose
face she had never seen,
she harbored loneliness at
his absence and
resentment over the
hardships he had caused
her grandfather and
mother. Later, even when
Orson told her that the
Anomaly Chiram was
targeting was in fact her
real father, her
long-nurtured anger made
her stubbornly deny it.
When she heard that Kei
had fathered a child with
Mimsy, her irritation only
grew. However, when the
mission to protect the
Anomaly was later handed
down, she suppressed her
personal feelings and
faithfully carried out the
mission. During that time
the awkward parent and
child clashed repeatedly,
each time drawing sighs
from Orson. But when she
was wounded, Kei was
there at her bedside,
devoting himself to her
care. That incident
seemed to dissolve the ill
will, and when she sortied
again, she wore Emaan
clothes instead of the
Chiram military uniform.
Just before Kei plunged
into the Great Anomaly,
she at last called him
'Father' and handed him a
pendant containing a
photo of Tina. At the
same time, she had been
entrusted by Orson with
his sunglasses as a
keepsake.

A young man belonging
to the Free Space Force.
Twenty years old.
 In the year 2062, before
the world descended into
spacetime chaos, he
fought alongside his best
friend Kei as a team.
 Serious and strongly
responsible almost to the
point of rigidity, he
seems every inch the
soldier, but only when
together with Kei did he
ever let his youthful
true self show.
 Caught in the explosion
of the spacetime
vibration bomb that Kei
set off, he became a
second Anomaly and was
cast fifteen years into
the future.

A young man who came
to be known as the other
Anomaly in a world sealed
within the Realm of
Conflict.
 He was born the same
year as Kei, but because
he appeared in the
chaotic spacetime five
years earlier, his lived
age is also five years

twenty-five.
 When he appeared in the
Chaos Century, he came
under the protection of
Chiram army General
Michael Henderson. Through
that connection he met
the general's beloved
daughter Tina, and
likewise his granddaughter
Athena. After Tina and

Mu attack, he became

instructor, supporting her

 In recognition of his

A young man who came
to be called the other
Anomaly in a world sealed
by the clashing spheres.
He was born in the same
year as Kei, but having
appeared in the Chaotic
Time-Space five years
earlier than Kei, his lived
age was also five years
older, making him 25. Upon
appearing in the Chaotic
Time-Space Century, he
was taken under the
protection of General
Michael Henderson of the
Chiram military. Through
that connection he met
the general's beloved
daughter Tina and his
granddaughter Athena.
After Tina and Michael
died in a Mu attack, he
became Athena's guardian
and instructor, supporting
her in both public and
private matters without
ever revealing his hidden
feelings. As a key figure
known as the Anomaly,
and with his pre-Chaotic
Time-Space achievements
recognized, he received
the unprecedented rank of
Special Major General in
the Chiram military. He
initially clashed with Kei
as well, but once Chiram
pushed forward with a
space-time repair plan
that did not use the
Anomaly, he left the
military and returned to
sharing the same pot of
rice with Kei again. In
the end he entered the
Great Anomaly together
with Kei and confronted
his past self, pulling the
trigger to bring an end
to the chaos. Among the
infinite possibilities of
the future shown in the
epilogue, there was also a
scene of him exchanging a
kiss with Athena.

Commander of the Chiram
army's Tran Garrison. His
rank is Captain.
 As a battle-hardened
veteran, he is the type
to fixate on honors and
military achievements.
 He initially acted to
capture Kei, the Anomaly,
but his objective later
shifted to assassination
following a change in
orders. He continued to
relentlessly pursue Kei,
including the traitor
Orson, but failed time
and again.
 When he proved unable
to complete his mission
and was about to be
relieved of command, he
and his subordinates
confronted his superior
officer Wesley and
pleaded for the mission
to continue. Given one
last chance, he set out
for the front line
himself.

Commander of the Chiram
military's Tran garrison.
His rank is Captain. As a
veteran of many battles,
he is the type to cling
to honors and military
achievements. Initially he
acted to seize Kei, the
Anomaly, but as orders
changed his objective
shifted to assassination.
He persistently pursued
both Kei and Orson, who
had become a traitor, but
each time he met with
failure. About to be
removed from his command
for his constant inability
to complete his mission,
he pressed his superior
Wesley along with his
subordinates, pleading for
the mission to continue.
Seizing his last chance,
he went to the front
lines himself. In the
decisive battle fought
with his back to the wall,
he launched a fierce
assault on Manisha's
fleet, which was trying
to protect Kei and Orson,
but was shot down by
Orson, who had sortied
out. He was persuaded to
reconsider Plan D but
would not listen, and as
he was regrouping for
another attack he took
the main cannon of the
Gargos, entrusted his
legacy to Henry, and died
in the explosion.

Deputy commander of the
Chiram army's Tran
Garrison.
 Calm and composed, he
ably assists Commander
Roberto, whom he holds in
high esteem. He always
takes the lead in the
operations to capture the
Anomaly, but fails time
and again.
 When he and Roberto
were about to be pulled
from the mission, he
pressed their superior
officer Wesley - in
something close to a
threat - to let them
continue, and won one
last chance.

Deputy commander of the
Chiram military's Tran
garrison. Calm and
composed by nature, he
ably supported his beloved
commander Roberto. In the
operation to seize the
Anomaly he always led
from the front, but
failures piled up. When he
was about to be relieved
of his post, he
half-coerced his superior
Wesley into allowing the
mission to continue, and
seized the last chance.
But in the desperate
final battle he lost
Roberto and was forced
into a bitter retreat.
Afterwards he showed his
obsession by deserting
the military to continue
chasing Kei and Orson. He
launched an attack after
Emaan and Chiram had
formed a joint force, but
a missile strike from a
force dispatched by
Wesley brought him down
with his goal unachieved.

Shaya's twin younger
sister.
 Since her older sister,
who should rightfully be
head of the family, is
off on a carefree trading
journey, Manisha has
become the de facto head
of the Tobu family in her
place.
 She clashed with the
Raas family, Mimsy's
household, over how to
handle Kei, and asked him
to help repair the
spacetime chaos with the
Emaan at its center. Her
heavy-handed approach,
however, provoked
resistance, and her
proposal was refused. She
then showed herself
willing to go so far as
to brainwash Kei, which
put her at odds with her
own sister as well.

Manisha Tove is Shaya's
twin sister. Her elder
sister, who should be the
head of the family, is
away on a wandering
merchant's journey, so
Manisha serves as the de
facto head of the Tove
household in her place.
She came into conflict
with Mimsy's family, the
Lars household, over the
treatment of Katsuragi,
and asked Katsuragi to
undertake time-space
restoration centered on
Emaan. However, her
forceful methods provoked
resistance, and her
proposal was refused.
When she then showed a
willingness to brainwash
Katsuragi, she came into
conflict with her own
sister as well. She
continued to pursue
Glomar afterward, but was
shocked when Mimsy
revealed that her husband
Lanch had once favored
Shaya, and that Shaya
had stepped aside for
Manisha's sake.
Furthermore, at a
discussion meeting, she
heard her sister's sincere
words that saving the
Earth should take priority
over Emaan's future, and
at last she was
reconciled with Shaya.

President of Chiram and
supreme commander of its
military. His full name is
Jeffrey White.
 He issued the order to
capture the Anomaly in
order to repair the
chaotic spacetime world
and erase Mu, Chiram's
greatest enemy. He later
pushed forward 'Plan D,' a
scheme to repair the
world by artificially
triggering another
spacetime vibration
through mechanical means.
 Even as he offered
peace, he secretly plotted
to brainwash Kei and
Orson, hiding a
ruthlessness that will
order any means
necessary to achieve his
ends. Yet everything he
does is for the greater
cause of Chiram's
survival, and he himself
is a selfless man.

 He moved to relieve

Wesley is the commander
of the Chiram military's
front-line base, with the
rank of lieutenant
general. He attempted to
relieve Roberto's team of
their mission to eliminate
the Anomaly after their
repeated failures, but
gave them one last
chance after receiving a

Emaan and Chiram formed

appeared intent on
destroying the Anomaly
even at the cost of
breaking from military
control, so Wesley
dispatched reinforcements
and had him eliminated.

A young scientist living
on Planet S-1. Twenty
years old.
 Alongside his father, Dr.
Reigan, and his colleagues,
he worked on developing a
radiation filtration and
circulation system to
save Planet S-1 from
radioactive contamination.
However, Gattler's faction
framed him for the
emperor's assassination
and executed his father
and colleagues in a coup.
In the process, Marin
killed Aphrodia's younger
brother Milan, and he and
Aphrodia became bitter
enemies, each hating the
other as the one who
took someone dear to
them.
 He boarded the
Pulsarvern, a
subspace-capable
spacecraft his father had
developed, and pursued
Gattler, but was caught
up in the warp of a
subspace fortress and
crash-landed on the
surface of the moon. He
was taken prisoner by
Blue Fixer while lying
unconscious. Because he
holds an intense longing
for the nature already
lost on Planet S-1, when
he first saw Earth's
oceans and skies, their
beauty moved him to
tears.
 He was originally an
approachable, cheerful,
and likeable young man,
but the string of
misfortunes he suffered,
combined with the
frustration of not being
trusted by those around
him, sometimes led him to
lash out at Blue Fixer
members in fits of rage.
 He later volunteered to
join Blue Fixer in order
to defeat his archenemy
Gattler, and with the
birth of Baldios, he
gradually began to open
his heart to his fellow
Blue Fixer members.
