A special member of Blue
Fixer's Special Task
Force, and the pilot of
the New Pulsarvern and
Baldios.
 Because he is an alien,
he was at first suspected
of being a spy and met
with strong resistance
within the base. But
through his own actions
he gradually won the
crew's trust, and his
outstanding piloting skill
and knowledge of subspace
mechanics eventually
earned him the position
of Baldios's main pilot.
 He holds firmly to the
belief that whatever he
judges to be right must
be carried out, and he
will rush to the aid of
comrades or loved ones in
danger even at the cost
of violating orders. But
that conviction is a
double-edged sword that
can also become a
liability - as shown when
he was prepared to kill
Marie, the news director
of World Broadcasting, to
protect Baldios's secret
when she tried to uncover
the truth about the Blue
Fixer base.
 At heart, though, he is
a pure-hearted young man
who secretly loves
Earth's beauty even more
than Earth's own people
do. Precisely because of
this, his determination to
defeat Gattler is fierce,
and his anger toward
Aldebaron, which seeks to
engulf Earth in war,
burns like a raging fire
within him.
 He seems to be hopeless
when it comes to
romance: when Jamie
invited him to a concert,
he showed up at the
meeting place with Raita
and Oliver in tow, an
oblivious response that
hurt her feelings.
 Though he and Aphrodia
remain enemies, their
exchanges through battle
seem to have struck a
chord somewhere in his
heart.

Marin Reigan is a special
member of Blue Fixer's
special combat unit and
the pilot of New
Palsaverne and Baldios. As
an alien, he was initially
suspected of being a spy
and faced strong hostility
within the base. However,
through his actions he
gradually won trust, and
with his superior piloting
skill and knowledge of
subspace mechanics, he
was finally made the main
pilot of Baldios. He is a
man of conviction who
always carries out what
he believes is right, and
he will rush to the aid
of comrades and loved
ones in crisis even at
the cost of disobeying
orders. But that
conviction is a
double-edged sword that
can also become a
liability. This was
revealed when he was
willing to kill Marie, the
news bureau chief of the
world broadcast, to
protect the secret of
Baldios when she tried to
investigate the Blue Fixer
base. In truth, however,
he is a pure-hearted
young man who loves the
beauty of the Earth more
than Earthlings
themselves. For that very
reason, his obsession with
defeating Gattler is
fierce, and his anger
toward Aldebaron, who
would engulf the Earth in
war, burns like a raging
fire within his heart. He
seems oblivious in matters
of love: when Jamie
invited him to a concert,
he showed up at the
meeting place with Raita
and Oliver in tow, hurting
her feelings with such a
careless response. Though
he was opposed to
Aphrodia, their exchanges
through battle touched a
chord in his heart. In
time, his heart was drawn
toward her, but the war
would claim Aphrodia's
life. In the unaired final
episode of the TV series,
after parting from
Gattler as they departed
for a new star, he
returned alone to Earth,
where he was greeted by
the phantoms of Aphrodia
and Raita. In the
theatrical version, after
descending to a Earth
polluted by radiation, he
cradled the lifeless
Aphrodia in his arms and
walked toward the
lighthouse where the two
had apparently first met.

A corporal in Blue
Fixer's Special Task Force
and pilot of the Baldy
Prize. Twenty-two years
old.
 Born in the slums, he
was placed in a care
facility together with his
younger sister Emily
after their parents
separated when he was
ten. He volunteered for
the Blue Fixer Youth
Corps at twelve, and it
was there that he met
Raita, who has been his
best friend ever since.
 Cheerful and quick to
show his feelings, he has
the temperament of a
delinquent who won't back
down from anything he
can't stand. When he was
captured by Aldebaron and
nearly turned into a spy
with a mind control
device, he cut himself
with a knife rather than
lose himself, holding on
to his sanity through
sheer resistance. Having
survived a poor and rough
childhood, he also
exploded with anger at
the World Federation's use
of force to put down
rioters when Aldebaron's
destruction of Earth's
crops caused a food
shortage, and personally
led an assault on the
Federation's warehouses.
 Yet he is by no means a
crude man: he keeps a
Bible close at hand as his
constant companion, and
he has quietly continued
to carry a torch for
Jamie, hinting at an
innocent side beneath the
surface.

Oliver Jack is a corporal
in Blue Fixer's special
combat unit and the pilot
of Baldiprize. He is 22
years old. Born in a slum,
his parents separated
when he was ten, so he
and his younger sister
Emily were placed in an
institution. He volunteered
for the Blue Fixer Boys'
Corps at age twelve, and
Raita, whom he met there,
has been his close friend
ever since. He is cheerful
and wears his emotions on
his sleeve, with a
delinquent streak, and he
will resist to the end
anything he cannot
stomach. When captured
by Aldebaron and nearly
turned into a spy through
a mind-control device, he
resisted by cutting
himself with a knife to
stay sane. Having survived
a poor and turbulent
boyhood, when Aldebaron
withered the Earth's
crops and caused food
shortages, he erupted in
anger at the World
Federation's methods of
suppressing rioters by
force, and led an attack
on the Federation's
warehouses himself. Yet
he is by no means a
crude person: he keeps
a Bible at hand as his
treasured companion and
secretly harbors feelings
for Jamie, revealing a
pure side. When
Aldebaron's plan to
destroy humanity brought
a great flood upon the
Earth, he trembled with
frustration at being
unable to save Emily and
her family, and wept
alone over her letter.

A sergeant in Blue
Fixer's Special Task Force
and pilot of the
Caterranger. Twenty-one
years old. He also works
as a part-time
night-school instructor at
the military academy.
 He hails from Little
Japan, a facility built at
point M-29 on the moon,
and is the sole survivor
of a spaceship accident
that wiped out all its
other residents. He was
raised afterward in a
care facility, enlisted in
the Blue Fixer Youth
Corps at eleven, and went
on through the military
academy before joining
the Blue Fixer forces.
 A stubborn man of
simple, sturdy virtue and
deep feeling. He refuses
to let others take on
dangerous missions in his
place, and is himself the
brave sort who volunteers
first.
 When Marin first joined
the unit, Raita did not
trust him at all, and
their exchanges often
escalated from verbal
spats into outright
fistfights. But as they
weathered life-and-death
situations together, Raita
came to feel Marin's
resolve firsthand and
grew to trust him
completely.

Raita Hokuto is a
sergeant in Blue Fixer's
special combat unit and
the pilot of the
Catallenger. He is 21
years old and also serves
as a part-time instructor
at the military academy's
night school. He is from
the facility 'Little Japan'
built at point M-29 on
the Moon, and is the sole
survivor of a spaceship
accident that killed all
aboard. Raised afterward
in a foster home, he
joined the Blue Fixer
Boys' Corps at age
eleven, went through the
military academy, and was
assigned to the Blue
Fixer unit. He is a
stubborn man of solid
character and deep
sentiment, who dislikes
sending others on
dangerous missions and
bravely volunteers
himself. When Marin first
joined the unit, Raita did
not trust him at all, and
their arguments often
escalated into fistfights.
However, as they faced
death together, he came
to feel Marin's resolve
firsthand and trusted him
from the bottom of his
heart. In the unaired
episode 38, he went to
deal with nuclear missiles
seized by the enemy,
completed the mission, but
was fatally wounded by
Gattler's attack. Despite
his efforts, Gattler,
fearing Baldios, launched
the remaining nuclear
missiles, and the Earth
was polluted with
radiation.

A staff member of the
Applied Physics Laboratory
within Blue Fixer's Science
Development Bureau.
Eighteen years old.
 She lived alone with her
mother from a young age,
but after her mother's
death she was raised by
a Greek family of
Japanese descent.
Following her adoptive
parents' deaths she
entered a care facility,
and at fifteen
volunteered for the World
Federation Forces.
 She wears her emotions
plainly and cannot bring
herself to abandon
someone in trouble. She
normally works under
Quinstein, but she is an
active young woman who,
depending on the mission,
willingly joins Marin and
the others in actual
combat.
 Her father's identity
was unknown, but during a
mission to the Kingdom of
Bard, it came to light
that the King of Bard
himself was her father.
 That she was convinced
early on that Marin could
be trusted shows just
how perceptive she truly
is. Perhaps it was
inevitable that, in
touching and gently
unraveling his pure but
lonely heart with her
compassion, she should
gradually find herself
drawn to him.

Jemmy Hoshino is an
18-year-old member of
the applied physics
research laboratory
belonging to the science
development bureau of the
World Federation's Blue
Fixer. From a young age,
she lived alone with her
mother, but after her
mother's death, she was
raised by a
Japanese-Greek family.
After the death of her
foster parents, she
entered an institution,
and at age 15 volunteered
for the World Federation
military.
 Her emotional expressions
are clear and direct, and
she cannot abandon people
in need. She normally
works under Quinstein,
but depending on the
mission, she is an active
girl who willingly joins
Marin and the others in
actual combat.
 Her father's identity
was unknown, but during a
mission to the Bird
Kingdom, the truth came
to light that the Bird
King was in fact her
father.
 Her early conviction
that Marin was a
trustworthy person shows
that she possesses
extremely keen sensibility.
It may have been
inevitable that, through
her loving care touching
his pure and lonely heart
and gradually untangling
it, she came to be drawn
to him. However, since
Marin always had his eyes
on Aphrodia, her romantic
feelings never came to
fruition.

Commander-in-chief of
Blue Fixer, an independent
organization under the
World Federation. Forty
years old. He formerly
served as director of the
World Federation's Far
East Branch.
 He initially treated
Marin as a suspected spy,
but was moved by Marin's
love for Earth and
welcomed him into Blue
Fixer as a fellow fighter.
 Owing to his position, he
tends to be excessively
hard on himself - even
when word came of danger
to the wife and child he
had left behind in Japan,
he suppressed his urge to
go help them and tried to
ignore it. He is also a
good leader with the
fairness to speak his
mind, undeterred by rank
or position, whenever
someone is clearly in the
wrong.
 He shows real concern
for his subordinates as
well, such as throwing
birthday parties to
reward the hard-worked
Blue Fixer members. To
his troops, he is equal to
a father as much as a
commanding officer. Away
from work, though, he is
an ordinary middle-aged
man whose hobbies are
watching classic films and
jogging every morning.

Takeshi Tsukikage is the
commander of Blue Fixer,
an independent organ of
the World Federation. He
is 40 years old and
formerly served as chief
of the World Federation
Far East branch.
 Initially treating Marin
as a spy, he was moved
by Marin's feelings for
Earth and welcomed him
into Blue Fixer as a
comrade in arms.
 His position tends to
make him too hard on
himself - even when news
of his wife and children's
crisis in Japan arrived,
he suppressed his desire
to rescue them and tried
to ignore it. He is also a
good leader with the
fairness to voice his
opinions without fear of
rank or position when
someone clearly acts
wrongly.
 He also showed
consideration for his
subordinates, such as
holding birthday parties
to reward the
hard-working Blue Fixer
members. To the members,
he is not just a superior
but almost a father
figure. Away from work,
however, he is an
ordinary middle-aged man
whose hobbies are
watching classic films and
jogging every morning.
 In the unaired episode
34, he sortied in a Mini
Palsaburn to rescue Marin
and the others on a
suicide mission carrying
melted-down nuclear
material into subspace
from the undersea base
battle, saving both Earth
and the young people by
ramming the Spirit Gattler
I together with the
nuclear material.

A scientist with Blue
Fixer and director of its
Science Development
Bureau. Thirty-two years
old.
 As the leader supporting
Blue Fixer on the
technical side, she
developed a range of
mecha, chief among them
the Baldy Prize and
Caterranger. Most notable
is her analysis and
modification of the
Pulsarvern - the pinnacle
of Planet S-1's subspace
engineering - to build
Baldios, a feat of insight
and technical skill that
speaks to her
extraordinary ability and
expertise as a scientist.
 She once held a position
in a research lab at
Sunbridge University, but
resigned after the World
Federation ordered a halt
to joint research she was
conducting with her
mentor and lover, Nerudo,
on the grounds that it
risked being converted
into a weapon. She then
volunteered for the World
Federation Forces and has
devoted herself to
Earth's defense ever
since.
 A strong-willed, quiet
woman, she suppresses her
emotions and throws
herself into her duty.
Harsh with herself and
others alike, she shot
Nerudo without hesitation
when he misused the
'Vacuum Box,' one of her
own past research
achievements, as a
weapon. Yet her granting
the final wish of her
student David, who was
heading toward certain
death, shows that she is
without doubt a deeply
compassionate person
underneath.
 She also has a sharp
eye for talent: among
the crew members who
suspected Marin of being
an alien spy, she was the
first to recognize his
knowledge of subspace
mechanics and his high
piloting skill, and
requested his cooperation
as a pilot for Baldios.

Ella Quinstein is a
scientist attached to Blue
Fixer and director of the
science development
bureau. She is 32 years
old.
 As a leader supporting
Blue Fixer from the
technical side, she
developed various
machines, led by the
Baldiprize and Catallenger.
Most notably, her concept
and technical skill in
analyzing and modifying
the Palsaburn - the
culmination of subspace
engineering on Planet S-1
- to build Baldios shows
extraordinary scientific
ability and capability.
 She previously held a
post at the Sunbridge
University research
laboratory, but resigned
when the World Federation
issued a suspension order
for her joint research
with her mentor and lover
Nerd, citing 'risk of
military application.'
Afterward, she
volunteered for the World
Federation military and
has been devoting herself
to Earth's defense.
 She is a resolute and
quiet woman who
suppresses her emotions
and devotes herself to
her duties. She is strict
with both herself and
others, and did not
hesitate to shoot dead
Nerd when he misused her
earlier research
achievement, the 'Vacuum
Box,' as a weapon. Yet
she answered the final
wish of her student
Devitt heading toward
certain death, proving
without doubt that she is
truly a deeply emotional
person.
 Among members who
suspected Marin of being
an alien spy, she was
also one with a sure eye,
quickly recognizing his
knowledge of subspace
mechanics and high
piloting skill, and
requesting his cooperation
as Baldios' pilot.
 After Commander
Tsukikage's death, she
serves as acting
commander of Blue Fixer
to carry on his will. In
the theatrical version,
she boarded Baldios
together with Jemmy for
direct command in the
final battle at Saturn.

A pilot candidate for
Blue Fixer's Special Task
Force.
 He came to the Blue
Fixer base as second
pilot of the New
Pulsarvern. His nihilistic
air and provocative
manner make him easy to
misjudge, but underneath
he is a man with a
burning soul who will
readily throw his life
away for a cause he
believes in.
 He is Quinstein's former
student and has carried
romantic feelings for her
since his school days,
though he knows they can
never be returned, which
torments him.
 When Aldebaron moved
the moon Ganymede to
block out the sun, David
volunteered in Marin's
place to pilot the suicide
weapon Fixer 1 to destroy
it. His motive was not to
protect Earth, but to
protect Quinstein alone.
 Thanks to his looks and
the manner of his death,
he was a highly popular
character when the show
originally aired. In the
later theatrical film, he
is given noticeably
favorable treatment, even
briefly piloting Baldios.

Supreme
commander-in-chief of
Aldebaron. Twenty-five
years old.
 She lost her parents in
a traffic accident at
thirteen and was raised,
together with her younger
brother Milan, by Gattler.
She became captain of
Gattler's personal guard
at twenty-three and rose
to her current position
after the coup succeeded.
She holds strong trust
and loyalty toward
Gattler, and even when a
classmate from military
academy told her that it
was Gattler who had had
her parents assassinated,
her devotion never
wavered.
 Her skill as a commander
is exceptional; in
Gattler's stead, she
personally handles
everything from devising
strategy to directing
operations on the ground.
She also has a ruthless
side, having established a
merciless code under
which failure is paid for
with death, and having
lured and murdered those
who stood in the way of
herself or Gattler. Even
so, many resent that she
holds the post of
commander-in-chief simply
by virtue of being the
Fuhrer's trusted right
hand.
 When Marin killed her
beloved brother Milan
during the raid on the
Reigan Institute, she
came to hate him
intensely. Because of
this, she sometimes loses
her usual composure and
is swept away by raw
emotion whenever she
faces him.

Rosa Aphrodia is the
supreme commander of
Aldebaron. She is 25
years old.
 At age 13 she lost both
parents in a traffic
accident, and she and her
younger brother Milan
were raised by Gattler.
At 23 she became captain
of Gattler's palace guard,
and after the successful
coup she attained her
present position. She
holds strong trust and
loyalty toward Gattler,
and even when a
classmate from the
military academy told her
that Gattler had
assassinated her parents,
her heart never wavered.
 Her ability as a
commander is exceptional,
and she single-handedly
handles everything from
operational planning to
on-site command in
Gattler's place. She also
established the 'merciless
precept' that failure must
be atoned with death, and
has a cold side that
traps and murders those
who stand in her and
Gattler's way. However,
many resent that she
holds the position of
supreme commander merely
as the Fuhrer's
confidante.
 When the Reigan research
institute was attacked,
her beloved younger
brother Milan was killed
by Marin, and she came
to hate him fiercely. As
a result, when facing
Marin she would forget
her usual composure and
be swept away by
passion.
 Yet as she came into
contact with Marin's
purity in battle, she
gradually began to feel
something stronger than
hatred. As those feelings
swelled, her heart
wavered between her duty
as supreme commander, her
reverence for Gattler,
and her love-hate toward
Marin.
 In the unaired portion
of the TV version, she
was driven from Aldebaron
by Negroth's treachery,
and challenged battle
alone to exact revenge
but was defeated. In the
later theatrical version,
she was taken prisoner by
Blue Fixer but escaped
and vanished, only to
appear at the final
battle in the subspace
fortress, where she killed
Gattler with her own
hands. And while the
paths differed, in both
versions she drew her
last breath in the arms
of the Marin she loved.

Fuhrer of the Aldebaron
military. He also holds
the concurrent posts of
Chairman of the
Unification Council and
Chairman of the Joint
Chiefs, making him the de
facto dictator ruling the
people of Planet S-1.
Thirty-eight years old.
 Not only does he
possess exceptional
ability as a soldier, but
his charisma and drive let
him win the hearts of the
populace in an instant,
marking him as a leader
of considerable stature.
 On Planet S-1, he served
as captain of Emperor
Torinomias III's personal
guard and repeatedly
petitioned for an escape
from the
radiation-contaminated
planet. But growing
impatient with the
emperor, who deferred to
the scientists working
toward restoring the
environment, he used the
Aldebaron military to
carry out the emperor's
assassination. He then
pinned the blame on Marin
and had the scientists,
who stood in his way,
executed.
 After the coup
succeeded, he declared an
evacuation from Planet
S-1, loading the citizenry
aboard the giant
battleship Algol and
carrying out a warp to a
new world. Upon finding
Earth, the first habitable
planet discovered, he
decided to make it their
new homeworld and ordered
an attack to exterminate
humanity.
 Though generous toward
his own people, he has a
ruthless side as well,
unhesitatingly discarding
subordinates who fail him
if it serves his goals.
But even this stems from
the mission he set for
himself - saving the
people of Planet S-1 -
and his iron will never
wavered to the end.
 He dotes on Aphrodia,
both his subordinate and
something of a surrogate
daughter, and places
immense trust in her. He
has entrusted her with
full authority over the
invasion of Earth, while
he himself waits in the
subspace fortress for
word of the operation's
success.

Zeo Gattler is the
supreme commander of the
Aldebaron military. He
also holds the positions
of chairman of the
unified council and
chairman of the joint
chiefs of staff, making
him the de facto dictator
who controls the S-1
people. He is 38 years
old.
 Not only does he
possess high ability as a
soldier, but his charisma
and drive allow him to
quickly win the hearts of
the people, and he is a
leader of considerable
caliber.
 On planet S-1, he served
as captain of the imperial
guard for Emperor
Trinomias III, and
repeatedly petitioned for
escape from the
radiation-contaminated
planet. However, impatient
with the emperor, who
respected the opinions of
scientists seeking to
restore the environment,
he used the Aldebaron
military to carry out the
emperor's assassination.
He then framed Marin for
the crime and had the
troublesome scientists
executed.
 After the success of
the coup, he declared the
evacuation of S-1, loaded
the citizens aboard the
giant battleship Algol,
and carried out a warp to
a new world. When he
decided to make Earth,
the first habitable planet
discovered, their new
home world, he ordered an
attack to exterminate the
human race.
 He is tolerant of his
allies, but he also has a
heartless side, not
hesitating to discard
failed subordinates to
accomplish his goals. But
this too was for the
mission he had imposed
upon himself to save the
S-1 people, and his steel
will was never bent to
the very end.
 He dotes on Aphrodia,
who is both his
subordinate and like a
daughter to him, and
places immense trust in
her. For this reason, he
entrusted her with full
authority over the Earth
invasion, while he himself
awaited news of the
operation's success in a
subspace fortress.
 Later, however, taking
over from Aphrodia who
was having difficulty
conquering Earth, he took
command of a grand
scheme to annihilate
humanity by melting the
polar ice caps and
submerging the land. When
the resulting rise in sea
level made Earth's
geography resemble S-1
exactly, even the bold
man could not hide his
surprise.
 In the unaired episode
featuring the Saturn
decisive battle, he lost
most of the S-1 people
who had departed their
home world together.
Then, leading the few
compatriots remaining in
the cryogenic area, he
set off to search for a
new world.

A staff officer in the
Aldebaron military.
 Though outwardly
deferential to Gattler, he
is an ambitious man
scheming to topple him
from the Fuhrer's seat
and rise to the top of
Planet S-1's people should
the opportunity arise.
 He harbors a
deep-seated hatred for
Aphrodia, who let his twin
brother Garo die in the
Himalayas. Using the
relationship between Earth
and Planet S-1, a secret
Gattler keeps tightly
hidden, as leverage, he
pulled Aphrodia down from
her post as
commander-in-chief and
installed himself in her
place.

Negros is one of the
staff officers of the
Aldebaron military.
 He shows a posture of
submission to Gattler, but
he is an ambitious man
who schemes to topple
him from the position of
supreme commander and
stand at the apex of the
S-1 people, should the
opportunity arise.
 He deeply hates
Aphrodia, who left his
twin brother Gallo to die
in the Himalayas.
Therefore, using the
relationship between Earth
and S-1 that Gattler kept
hidden as a shield, he
dragged Aphrodia down
from her position as
commander-in-chief and
took her place.
 In the TV version, he
dies in an explosion from
Harman's suicide attack,
but in the theatrical
version he was given a
more important role. In
the final battle, even
with defeat certain, he
attempts to press the
nuclear missile launch
button to strike back at
the Earth side. This act
incurs Gattler's wrath,
and he is killed on the
spot. However, because he
fell onto the nuclear
missile launch button, the
missiles were launched.
The
radiation-contaminated
Earth began to transform
into a new S-1.

An Aldebaron officer who
secretly fed information
about his own side to
Blue Fixer.
 He has been Marin's
close friend since
childhood, having studied
together with him at UF
Museion, a university on
Planet S-1. However, a
rift formed in their
friendship over a matter
involving the awarding of
a degree, and Flick
disappeared from Marin's
life afterward.
 He currently serves in
the Aldebaron military,
waiting for a chance to
avenge comrades executed
during Aldebaron's coup.
After obtaining the
location of an important
secret factory, he sought
asylum on Earth and made
contact with Marin using
the battle mecha Silver
Shark. By the time the
two reunited, the old rift
between them was gone,
and they swore together
to defeat Gattler.

Flick Kyarin is an
Aldebaron officer who
secretly leaked allied
information to Blue Fixer.
 He was a childhood
friend of Marin, and the
two studied together at
UF Museion, the university
of planet S-1. However, a
dispute over the
acquisition of a
bachelor's degree put a
rift in his friendship
with Marin, and he
disappeared from Marin's
sight thereafter.
 Now, in order to avenge
the comrades who were
executed during the
Aldebaron coup, he
enlisted in the military
and awaited his chance
for revenge. When he
obtained the location of
an important secret
factory, he contacted
Marin, hoping to defect
to Earth. There was no
longer any discord
between the two upon
their reunion, and they
swore to each other to
defeat Gattler.
 However, the information
itself was a trap set by
Aphrodia, and the two
were trapped in a
hyper-warped space. To
save Baldios, he came up
with the idea of using
the explosion of Silver
Shark to erase the
distortion, and
deliberately played the
villain, attacking Baldios.
Though Marin knew his
friend's true intent, he
was left with no choice
but to go along with it,
and Silver Shark was
destroyed by Marin's
hand, allowing Baldios to
escape by the skin of its
teeth.

Emperor of Planet S-1.
 A gentle man by nature,
he supported the group
of scientists working to
restore the
radiation-contaminated
environment.
 However, under pressure
from the military at the
Supreme Council, Gattler
forced him to agree that
if the radiation filtration
and circulation system
was not completed within
a set deadline, the
military would be
dispatched to another
planet.
 But this was not enough
to satisfy Gattler, who
secretly plotted a coup.
On the very night the
system was completed, the
emperor was assassinated
in his bedroom by
Aphrodia, acting under
secret orders.

Emperor of Planet S-1.
 A gentle man by nature,
he supported the group
of scientists working to
restore the
radiation-contaminated
environment.
 However, under pressure
from the military at the
Supreme Council, Gattler
forced him to agree that
if the radiation filtration
and circulation system
was not completed within
a set deadline, the
military would be
dispatched to another
planet.
 But this was not enough
to satisfy Gattler, who
secretly plotted a coup.
On the very night the
system was completed, the
emperor was assassinated
in his bedroom by
Aphrodia, acting under
secret orders.

The second son of the
Jin family and main pilot
of Zambot 3. Twelve
years old, a first-year
middle school student.
 A local delinquent
notorious for constant
fighting and riding a
motorcycle without a
license, but at heart he
is kind and cannot bear
to leave anyone in
trouble.
 Using piloting knowledge
learned through
sleep-learning, along with
his natural athleticism
and sharp instincts, he
handles the Zambird,
Zambo Ace, and Zambot 3
as extensions of his own
body. Even so, he grew
increasingly frustrated
that the people around
him failed to understand
him despite his desperate
fight against the Gaizock.
But through witnessing
the Gaizock's escalating
campaign of destruction
and merciless tactics like
human bombs, and through
reconciling with those he
had clashed with, he grew
as a person.

Kamikita Kappei is the
second son of the
Kamikita family and the
main pilot of Zambot 3.
He is 12 years old and a
first-year middle school
student.
 He is a well-known
delinquent in his area,
spending his days fighting
and riding motorcycles
without a license.
However, his nature is
kind, and he is a man of
sentiment who cannot
ignore those in trouble.
 With piloting skills
acquired through sleep
learning, his natural
athleticism, and his keen
intuition, he controls
Zambird, Zambo Ace, and
Zambot 3 as if they were
parts of his own body. He
grew increasingly
frustrated, however, that
even as he desperately
fought Gaizock, the
people around him would
not understand. But
through witnessing the
escalating destruction and
inhuman tactics such as
human bombs, and through
reconciling with those he
had clashed with, he grew
as a person.
 In the final battle, even
reduced to Zambo Ace
alone, he destroyed
Gaizock and, unconscious,
returned alone to his
birthplace. He awoke in
the lap of Michi amid a
cheering crowd, gazing up
at a universe where war
was no more.

The eldest son of the
Kamie family and pilot of
the Zambull. Fifteen years
old, a third-year middle
school student.
 He has a cynical air and
look about him, but like
Kappei, he is warmhearted
underneath. Intelligent
and quick-witted, he
sometimes devised
strategies that
contributed to victory. He
has a younger brother
named Kazuyuki and a
younger sister named
Kiiro, both of whom look
up to him as a good older
brother.
 Unlike the other Jin
Family households, his has
what might be called an
overbearing 'education
mom' for a mother, one
who tries to protect only
her own life and
possessions with no
regard for those around
her, and Uchuta felt a
sense of guilt over this.
He once clashed with
Kappei after Kappei
mocked him for it, but
the two deepened their
bond through the fighting
that followed.

Kamikita Uchuta is the
eldest son of the
Kamikita family and the
pilot of Zambull. He is 15
years old and a
third-year middle school
student.
 He has a cynical air and
appearance, but like
Kappei, his nature is
warm. He is intellectual
and quick-witted, and on
occasion contributed to
victory by devising
strategies. He has a
younger brother named
Kazuyuki and a younger
sister named Kiiro, and
both look up to him as a
good older brother.
 Unlike the rest of the
Kami family, he has a
mother who could be
called a 'pushy mother',
and he felt a sense of
debt toward her for
trying to protect only
her own life and
household possessions
without regard for the
situation around them. He
clashed with Kappei over
this, but through battle
their bond deepened.
 In the final battle,
caught in Bandock's
ferocious assault and
realizing that neither he
nor his machine would
last much longer, he and
Keiko made a suicide
charge at the thruster
nozzles to open a path.
Even facing death, he
showed a kindness that
put others before himself,
apologizing to Keiko that
if he had only moved
alone, she would not have
been caught up in it.
Then, amid the rising
debris, crying out
Kappei's name as if
entrusting his feelings to
him, he vanished into
space.

The eldest daughter of
the Kamikita family and
pilot of the Zambase. A
second-year middle school
student, thirteen years
old through episode
eleven.
 Her family runs a ranch
in Shinshu, and she is a
beautiful, lively, and
easygoing girl whose
talents are horseback
riding and archery. She
has a younger sister
named Kimiko, who is
introverted and bears no
resemblance to her, in
either looks or
personality.
 When she returned to
her hometown for her
birthday, she, like the
other members of the Jin
Family, was resented by
her old friends for
reasons that were not
her fault, and was shown
to have a vulnerable side,
taking the rejection hard.
But drawing strength from
her mother's feelings, she
recovered, and her friends
came to see the truth
and reconcile with her
after witnessing her
continue rescue efforts
even while wounded by
stray gunfire. This inner
strength is truly her
defining trait.

She is the eldest
daughter of the Kamikita
family and the pilot of
the Zambe Base. She is a
13-year-old (until
episode 11) second-year
middle school student. Her
family runs a ranch in
Shinshu, and her
specialties are horseback
riding and archery, making
her an active and
generous beautiful girl.
She has a younger sister
named Kimiko, but Kimiko
is introverted and
completely unlike her in
appearance.
 On her birthday, when
she returned to her
hometown, she was
resented by her friends
like the other Kam family
members, and showed
weakness in being shocked
by this. However, she
recovered through her
mother's love, and her
figure continuing rescue
operations despite
injuries from stray
bullets led her friends to
clear up their
misunderstandings and
approach her. This inner
strength is her true
essence.
 During the decisive
battle against Bandock,
when she saw that combat
with Zambot 3 was
impossible, she detached
the still-functional Zambo
Ace and, along with
Uchuta, carried out a
suicide attack on the
thruster port to open a
path. Even at the brink
of death, she showed
composure in admonishing
Uchuta, who apologized
for involving her in the
attack. But in her final
moments, there was the
figure of a girl her age
calling out her father's
and mother's names.

Keiko's grandfather.
Seventy-five years old.
 As something of an elder
statesman of the Jin
Family, he holds the group
together with strong will
and conviction as they
face the Gaizock.
 He and Umee, a trusted
advisor to the family, are
cousins, but the fact
that he once gave her a
rice bowl as a gift in his
younger days suggests
there may have been
something more between
them.
 He also provides the
narration for the
next-episode previews,
memorably closing each
one with the line, "Now
then, how will they fight
their way through this
time?"

He holds the position of
elder of the Kam family,
uniting the clan under
strong will and conviction
as they face the battle
against Gaizock. He and
Umee, a good advisor, are
cousins, and the fact
that he gave her a tea
bowl in his youth
suggests they were quite
close. In the end, he
carried out a suicide
attack against Bandock in
Beal II alongside Umee to
save King Beal from
crisis. Entrusting the
future to the younger
generation, he closed the
curtain on his life. He
also handled the narration
for the next episode
previews, and his closing
line, 'Well then, how will
we fight through?' was
memorable. After his
suicide attack, the line
was changed to the
third-person perspective,
'Well then, how will they
fight?'

Kappei's father.
Forty-eight years old.
 A fishing boat owner
who runs Jin Fisheries in
Suruga Bay. After Beal I
was discovered, he took
command of it as its
captain during battle.
 Though strict by nature,
he holds deep love for
his wife and children, a
man of the sea
overflowing with warmth
and manly spirit. Having
often been away from
home for deep-sea
fishing, he knows well the
value of time spent
together with family.

Kappei's father. 48
years old. He is a fishing
fleet owner running Kami
Fisheries in Suruga Bay.
After Beal I was
discovered, he served as
its captain and directed
combat operations. Though
strict in character, his
love for his wife and
children runs deep, and he
is a man of the sea full
of tolerance and
gallantry. Because he was
often away from home for
deep-sea fishing, he knew
the importance of time
spent with family. His end
was a fierce one: he
rammed the Red Knight
Deathkaine and Blue
Knight Helldyne, taking
them with him and
protecting his beloved
wife to the last.

Kappei's older brother.
Seventeen years old.
 Serious and
mild-mannered in contrast
to his brother, he is in
charge of combat command
aboard Beal I and King
Beal.
 Possessed of sharp
insight, he discovered
Zambot 3's combination
system. At one point, to
discipline Kappei and the
others for their lack of
coordination, he brought
the Zambo Ace to a halt
and forced them to agree
to combine by
threatening, "If the Jin
Family can't fight without
unity, then we might as
well all die together" - a
bold and quick-witted
move on his part.

Kappei's older brother.
17 years old. In contrast
to his younger brother,
he has a serious and
gentle personality. He
handles combat command
for Beal I and King Beal.
He possesses sharp
insight and discovered the
combination system of
Zambot 3. On that
occasion, to admonish
Kappei and the others
who were not working
together, he stopped
Zambo Ace's movements
and threatened, 'Kappei
without solidarity and a
Kam family that cannot
fight are unnecessary, so
let's all die together,'
getting them to agree to
combine - a bold and
resourceful action. After
the conclusion with
Gaizock, he barely
survived, but he slowed
down Bandock as it
entered the atmosphere
using Beal I, and after
rescuing Kappei, who was
left behind inside, he
himself was swallowed by
the flames of the
explosion and departed
this world.

Kappei's grandmother.
Sixty-eight years old.
 She serves as an advisor
to the Jin Family, and
even Heizaemon places
complete trust in her.
 A spry old woman who
never seems her age, she
loves rock music and once
even suited up in battle
gear to sortie herself in
order to save Nozaki, her
first love.

Kappei's grandmother. 68
years old. She holds a
position of advisor to
the Kam family, and
Heizaemon places complete
trust in her. Her favorite
music is rock, and she
once donned a combat
suit and sortied out
herself to save Nozaki,
her first love - a
vigorous grandmother who
shows no signs of her
age. When she went into
space for the decisive
battle, she carried out a
suicide attack against
Bandock in Beal II
alongside Heizaemon to
save King Beal, which had
fallen into crisis.
Entrusting the future to
her grandchildren, she
lowered the curtain on
her life. Before that
sortie, she left behind
the tea bowl that
Heizaemon had given her
in her youth, a keepsake
of memories.

Kappei's mother.
Thirty-five years old.
 Bold and big-hearted,
just as she appears.
 Her love for her two
sons and her husband is
plain to see, and when
Kazuki fired a gun at her
out of misplaced
resentment, she showed
both strength and
motherly resolve by
slapping him without fear
of the weapon, setting
him straight.

Kappei's mother. 35
years old. She is a
boisterous and generous
woman, as her appearance
suggests. She shows love
for her two sons and
husband, and when Kazuki
fired a gun out of
misplaced resentment, she
did not fear the weapon
and slapped him,
displaying the strength
and maternal nature to
correct wrongdoings. Just
before the final battle
with Gaizock, she was
sent back to Earth by
the older men who did not
want women and children
involved in the fighting.
When Kappei survived the
battle and returned, she
rushed to his side.

Kappei's beloved dog,
named Nishiki for the
flower-petal pattern on
his forehead.
 He rides along with
Kappei in the Zambird's
right-hand cockpit during
sorties. In time he came
to take over Kappei's
'Woof!' call during
combination sequences.

Kappei's beloved dog. It
was named Chiyonishiki
after the flower-petal
pattern on its forehead.
When sortieing, it rides
in the right cockpit of
the Zambird alongside
Kappei. Eventually, it
came to handle Kappei's
shout of 'One!' during
combination. When Zambo
Ace penetrated the
interior of Bandock, it
was vaporized by a direct
hit from the laser of the
automatic defense system.

The leader of the
delinquent Kazuki Gang, a
boy who was at odds with
Kappei.
 In a Gaizock attack, he
was separated from his
parents and his younger
sister Kaoru. Believing
the Jin Family was to
blame, he harbored intense
hatred toward them.
 But after witnessing the
Gaizock's merciless
tactics, such as human
bombs, he gradually
changed his outlook. He
was later caught in a
crisis that nearly turned
him into a human bomb
himself, but escaped
thanks in part to
Kappei's efforts. When
the two were reunited,
they shared a heartfelt
handshake, and from then
on Kazuki cooperated with
Kappei, ultimately joining
the Jin Family in the
journey to space for the
final battle.

The leader of the
delinquent gang
Kazuki-gumi, which was in

was separated from his
parents and his younger
sister Kaoru. Believing
the Kami Family was
responsible for this, he
harbored intense hatred.
However, witnessing the
cruel tactics of the
Gaizock, such as human
bombs, he gradually
changed his views.
Eventually he found
himself in a crisis where
he nearly became a human
bomb himself, but escaped

efforts. After exchanging
a warm handshake with
the reunited Kappei, he
began to cooperate, and

Just before the final
battle with Gaizock, he
was sent back to Earth
by the older men who did
not want women and
children involved, and
upon waking he lamented

together. After the
battle ended and Kappei
returned, he was the
first to find him along
with Miti, and watched
over his sleeping face
trembling with fear.

A member of Kazuki's
delinquent gang, which was
at odds with Kappei.
 While evacuating
together with Kazuki and
the others, he was
captured by the Gaizock
and, without his
knowledge, converted into
a human bomb.

A member of the
delinquent gang
Kazuki-gumi, which was in
conflict with Kappei. While
evacuated with Kazuki and
the others, he was
captured by the Gaizock
and unknowingly modified
into a human bomb. He
tried to die in a place
where he would not cause
trouble to those around
him, but could not endure
the fear of dying alone
and went into a frenzy.
Restrained by others who
had also been made into
human bombs, he screamed
for help as he exploded.

A member of Kappei's
self-proclaimed honor
guard, nicknamed the
'Plain Pair.' She is 12
years old.
 Her family was caught in
a Gaizock attack, and her
mother suffered severe
injuries. Believing the Jin
family was to blame, Aki
vented her fierce anger
at Kappei. Deep down,
though, she understood
that Kappei and the
others were not truly at
fault, and with her
mother's encouragement
she gradually reconciled
with him.
 She was later captured
by the Gaizock, but
Kappei rescued her.

One of the members of
the so-called 'Bosu Pea',
Kappei's personal guard.
12 years old. She and her
family were caught in a
Gaizock attack and
suffered damage, with her
mother sustaining serious
injuries. She blamed the
Kami Family for this and
vented fierce anger at
Kappei. But deep down she
understood that the real
culprits were not Kappei
and the others, and with
her mother's words she
gradually reconciled.
Eventually she was
captured by the Gaizock,
but was rescued by
Kappei. However, by that
time, her body had
already been modified into
a human bomb. She was
brought to Kappei's room,
put on his pajamas, and
just when it seemed their
feelings would finally
unite, at the moment
before Kappei, alerted by
Heizaemon of the
possibility of a human
bomb, rushed to the room,
her body was enveloped in
light. All that remained
of her was a scrap of
pajama fabric in Kappei's
hand.

Another member of
Kappei's self-proclaimed
honor guard, one of the
so-called 'Plain Pair.'
 Her family was likewise
caught in a Gaizock
attack, and, convinced
that the Jin family was
responsible, she directed
her anger at Kappei.
 Like Aki, she was
captured by the Gaizock,
but Kazuki rescued her
before she could be
turned into a human bomb,
and she narrowly managed
to escape.

Michi is a member of
Kappei's guard, commonly
known as one of the 'Boo
Spare.' Her family was
caught in a Gaizock
attack and suffered
damage, and believing the
Kamikami family to be
responsible, she vented
her anger at Kappei. Like
Aki, she was captured by
Gaizock, but before being
turned into a human bomb,
she was rescued by
Kazuki's hand and
narrowly escaped. After
the battle ended, she
gently embraced Kappei,
who had returned to
Earth unconscious. At
that moment, her pent-up
feelings were pointed out
by Kazuki, and her cheeks
reddened.

Captain of the Bandock
and commander of the
Gaizock, a cyborg whose
body has been replaced
almost entirely with
machinery.
 Originally from a planet
on the frontier, he
became a servant of the
Gaizock god (Computer
Doll No. 8) and, on its
orders, schemes to
exterminate humanity.
 Cruel by nature and fond
of slaughter, he carries
out one atrocity after
another, including the
human bomb operations,
while at the same time
showing a strong interest
in Earth's culture and
entertainment.
 The object of his
interest changes
constantly - having a
designer tailor him
outfits, indulging in
pachinko, sunbathing, or
belting out songs with a
band - producing a
comical side wildly out of
balance with his
ruthlessness.

Killer the Butcher is the
captain of the Bandock
and the commander of the
Gaizock forces. He is a
cyborg whose body has
been almost entirely
replaced with machinery.
Originally from a frontier
planet, he became a
subordinate of the
Gaizock God (Computer
Doll No. 8) and,
following its instructions,
plotted the annihilation
of the human race. He
has a cruel personality
and treats slaughter as a
hobby, carrying out one
inhumane operation after
another, including human
bombs. At the same time,
he shows a strong
interest in Earth's
culture and entertainment.
His objects of interest
changed each time - he
had designers tailor
costumes for him, indulged
in pachinko, sunbathed,
and even formed a band
and sang passionately.
These comical aspects
stood in stark contrast
to his ruthlessness and
were seen on many
occasions. When the
Kamikami family closed in
on the Bandock at the
end of the fighting, he
separated the Bandock's
head and took to the
battlefield himself. Upon
receiving the Ion Cannon
from Zambot 3 and
realizing his defeat, he
left behind the parting
words that 'the Kamikami
family's fight is
meaningless' and crumbled
away.

A weapons officer of
the Gaizock.
 A schemer who proposes
various attacks to
Butcher. He also has a
foolish streak, however -
on one occasion his hand
slipped while trying to
press a missile launch
switch, setting off a
human bomb and blowing
himself up.

A weapons officer of
the Gaizock.
 A schemer who proposes
various attacks to
Butcher. He also has a
foolish streak, however -
on one occasion his hand
slipped while trying to
press a missile launch
switch, setting off a
human bomb and blowing
himself up.

An operations officer of
the Gaizock, in charge of
command at the front
lines.
 His large build and a
face crossed with
countless scars give him
a formidable, intimidating
look, but he shows
absolute obedience to
Butcher's orders.
 Confident but not much
of a strategist, he
sometimes cornered
Zambot 3 only to let
victory slip away at the
crucial moment.

 His large build and a

 Confident but not much

Zambot 3 only to let

The electronic brain at
the core of the Bandock,
and the true body of the
Gaizock.
 It had ceased activity
after destroying the
planet Vier 200 years
earlier. Upon approaching
Earth's sphere, it
reactivated its
programming and ordered
Butcher to annihilate the
human race.

Computer Doll No. 8 is
the electronic brain that
serves as the true body
of the Gaizock, residing
at the core of the
Bandock. After destroying
the planet Beal 200 years
ago, it halted its
activities. When it drew
near Earth's sphere, it
reactivated its program
and issued orders to
Butcher to eradicate
humanity. Its true nature
was an artificial
intelligence created long
ago by the Gaizock people
with the purpose of
driving out all beings
with malice throughout
the universe. Even when
it faced Zambo Ace after
losing the battle, it
continued to insist to
Kappei until the very end
that humanity was evil,
and then it collapsed.

The pilot of Daitarn 3,
known everywhere by his
nickname, 'Banjo Haran,
the Talk of the Town.' He
is 18 years old.
 Cheerful and upbeat,
brimming with humor, and
never without a joke even
in a crisis, he is a man
others can rely on. That
he never comes across as
smug despite his flashy,
self-assured manner is
thanks to the very human
side he lets show from
time to time.
 His physical abilities are
outstanding, allowing him
to hold his own against
Meganoids even unarmed.
His prowess is so great
that rumors occasionally
circulate that Banjo
himself might be a
Meganoid.
 He harbors fierce hatred
for the Meganoids, and
for his father, who
created them and used
Banjo's brother and
mother as test subjects.
He is ruthless enough to
accept the sacrifice of
his comrades if it means
destroying the Meganoids,
yet his friends still
place absolute trust and
affection in him
regardless.
 Note that the 'Haran
Conglomerate,' which
recurred throughout the
older Super Robot Wars
titles, is an original
setting created for the
games; in the anime
itself, he is simply
established as extremely
wealthy.

Banjo Haran is the pilot
of Daitarn 3. Known in all
places, he is the
so-called 'Legendary Banjo
Haran.' He is 18 years
old. Cheerful and bright,
full of a spirit of humor,
he is a reliable man who
never forgets a joke even
in a pinch. His conceited
and self-confident nature
does not come across as
unpleasant thanks to the
very human sides he
occasionally reveals. His
physical abilities are
outstanding, and he is
capable of fighting Mega
Noids on equal terms with
his bare body. Because of
his ferocity, rumors
sometimes circulate that
Banjo himself is a Mega
Noid. He fiercely hates
the Mega Noids and his
father, who created them
and used his older
brother and mother as
test subjects. He
possesses a ruthlessness
that would not hesitate
to sacrifice comrades in
order to destroy the
Mega Noids, yet his
comrades place tremendous
trust and affection in
him, including for that
very trait. During the
decisive battle against
Don Zauser, the leader of
the Mega Noids, Banjo
listened to the apology
of his creator but
rejected it, and alone
brought an end to his
feud with the Mega Noids.
Note that the 'Haran
Zaibatsu,' which
frequently appeared in
the old SRW series, is an
original game setting; in
the show itself, he
remains merely a very
wealthy man.

The butler in service to
Banjo. Age 55.
 From attending to
Banjo's daily needs, to
preparing meals and
maintaining various
machines, to even
sortieing in Daitarn 3
itself, he handles every
task flawlessly - a
butler among butlers.
 Nothing is known of his
background or past
history, but his great
skill and character have
earned him the complete
trust of Banjo and the
others.
 He is also a first-rate
marksman - so much so,
by his own account, that
people used to say,
"Wyatt Earp or Garrison?"

 From attending to

 Befitting her Interpol

Banjo's little brother
figure, a mischievous boy

 He lost his parents to

staying on as a

 He is known for his

 She is beautiful enough

 The pampered daughter

 She is beautiful enough

A Civilian boy who
single-mindedly pushes
forward, true to his own
convictions. He is 16
years old.
 He broke the 'Three-Day
Law' set down by the
Innocents, which held that
any crime became void
after three days had
passed, and kept pursuing
Timp, the man who killed
his parents. Along the
way he met Rag and the
others, and the group
tried together to steal a
Xabungle they happened to
spot. They ultimately
failed, but circumstances
afterward led him to come
aboard the Iron Gear.
 He is filled with a drive
that goes well beyond
mere initiative, and once
he sets his mind on
something he pushes
forward no matter what.
On the surface it looks
like nothing but
recklessness, but that
very attitude embodied
the 'strong Civilian' the
Innocents had longed for
across generations. His
influence spread to
others dissatisfied with
the status quo, and he
ultimately struck down
Cashim King, the root of
all the trouble.
 He is quite skilled at
piloting Walker Machines,
and even taught Blume
and the others at one
point. That said, his
teaching covered only the
basics - he seems to
have relied more on brute
force than fine technique
to get through most
situations.
 With his round face,
easygoing manner, and
rough, thoughtless
personality, he would not
seem, by ordinary
standards, to be popular
with girls. And yet,
perhaps because he was
unconventional in every
respect, he was quite
popular with the girls
around him.

Jiron Amos is a civilian
boy who charges forward
single-mindedly, faithful
to his own convictions. He
is 16 years old. Breaking
the 'Three-Day Law'
established by the
Innocent, which states
that any crime becomes
void after three days
have passed, he continued
to pursue Timp, the
murderer of his parents.
On the way, he met Rag
and the others, and
together they tried to
steal the Xabungle they
happened to come across.
Though they ultimately
failed, he subsequently
ended up boarding the
Iron Gear by
circumstance. He is full
of power that cannot be
contained by merely
calling him proactive -
once he sets his mind on
something, he charges
through to the end. At
first glance he seems
merely reckless, but that
very attitude was the
embodiment of the 'strong
civilian' that the
Innocent had longed for
over generations. That
influence spread to those
dissatisfied with the
current state of affairs,
and ultimately led to the
defeat of Kasim King, the
root of all evil. He is
quite skilled at piloting
Walker Machines, and he
sometimes even taught
Blume and the others.
However, that instruction
was only basic level;
more than excelling at
fine techniques, he more
often got through by
force. With his round
face, joker demeanor,
crude and thoughtless
personality, by any
ordinary standard he
hardly seems the type to
be popular with girls. Yet
perhaps because he was
unconventional in every
way, he was quite popular
with the girls around him.
However, when Arthur
appeared, he was suddenly
driven from that position.
After the defeat of the
Innocent, he made a manly
confession, declaring he
would become the eyes of
the blinded Elchi, and won
her heart. And then,
together with his
comrades, and those who
were not quite so, he
rode off across the
wasteland.

Captain of the Iron
Gear. Age 16. Her father,
the trading merchant
Carrying Cargo, died in
battle, leaving her to
inherit his position
against her own wishes.
 She admires the cultural
life of the Innocents and
dreams of bringing a
flowering of culture to
the surface world. She
herself, though, can
hardly be called ladylike
- she is quick-tempered
and handy with a throwing
knife, more tomboy than
lady. Even so, she seems
to be quite
self-conscious about her
personality deep down.
 She eventually falls for
the unconventional Jiron
and finds herself locked
in rivalry with Rag over
him.

Elchi Cargo is the
captain of the Iron Gear,
and she is sixteen years
old. Her father, the
trader Cargo, was killed
in battle, and against her
own wishes she was
forced to succeed him in
his role. She longs for
the cultured life of the
Innocent and dreams of
bringing the flower of
civilization to the earth.
However, she is hardly
what one would call
demure; rather, she is
quick-tempered and skilled
with throwing knives,
being more of a tomboy.
Even so, she seems to be
quite self-conscious about
her personality deep
down. Eventually she falls
in love with the
unconventional Jiron and
begins a rivalry with Rag
over him. Yet she is
abducted by the Innocent,
who have taken notice of
the new-age civilian, and
the personality of Kashiim
is implanted into her
brain. Under mental
control, Elchi becomes an
enemy of the Iron Gear
and stands in Jiron's path
time and again. When she
is finally rescued,
Arthur's desperate gambit
of drawing Kashiim's
personality into his own
brain restores her sense
of self, and with that
momentum she becomes one
of the causes that bring
an end to the era ruled
by the Innocent. After
the fighting concludes,
she is troubled by the
trouble she caused
everyone, and despite
having lost her sight as
an aftereffect of the
battle, she slips away
from the Iron Gear alone.
But the kindness and love
of Jiron, who pursues her,
touches her and shatters
her resolve to run away.

Helmsman and mechanic
of the Iron Gear.
 A rather nagging,
short-tempered man,
always shouting, his
outbursts were so much
like hysterics that people
called him 'Mr. Hysterics.'
 He has a deep love for
machines and absolute
confidence in his skill at
maintaining and handling
them. He has also been
quietly collecting
blueprints for the
machines purchased from
the Innocents, secretly
harboring the ambition of
one day building machines
with his own hands
without relying on the
Innocents.

Elchi's loyal servant and
bodyguard.
 He was once worked like
a slave under the corrupt
Lockman Gillan, until Elchi
bought his freedom. He
has sworn absolute
loyalty to her ever since.
 His basic physical
abilities are extremely
high, from the tremendous
strength his muscular
frame can unleash to his
surprising nimbleness.
When Elchi is in danger,
his abilities power up
even further, and he
displays superhuman
strength.

Fatman Big is Elchi's
loyal attendant and
bodyguard. He was once
forced to work like a
slave under the corrupt
locksmith Giran, until
Elchi bought him out.
Since then, he has sworn
absolute loyalty to her.
His physical abilities are
exceptional, including the
monstrous strength from
his muscular build and his
surprising agility. When
Elchi falls into crisis,
these abilities are
further enhanced, allowing
him to display superhuman
power. After Elchi is
taken by the Innocent, he
is even more determined
to fight for her sake,
and he boards the Gear
Gear alone to rescue her.
Even afterward, he
continues to interact
with Elchi through every
means available to him in
an effort to help her
regain her memories.

The female leader of the
bandit gang Sand Rat.
 While attacking a group
of Lockmen, she got help
from Jiron, who collapsed
nearby, and the two hit
it off. Lending him a
hand in stealing his
Xabungle drew her into
the affairs of the Cargo
family, and eventually her
whole team was hired on
aboard the Iron Gear.
 With a temperament,
nerve, and drive that put
most men to shame, she
is skilled not only at
piloting Walker Machines
but also at commanding
the Iron Gear whenever
Elchi is absent.
 She falls easily for
anyone who treats her
like a lady, Jiron chief
among them. She even
joined the self-styled
'Arthur Honor Guard,'
though Jiron remained her
true favorite.

A member of the bandit
gang Sand Rat. Age 15.
 A quick-draw expert and
a wisecracking cynic, he
plays it cool but is kind
at heart, hiding a
passionate spirit.
 He acts as something of
a sub-leader among the
members. In truth he is
in love with Rag, and
resents how attached she
has become to the
newcomer Jiron - a
grudge that once drove
him to leave the Iron
Gear.

A member of the bandit
gang Sand Rat. Age 16.
 Gentle and honest,
kind-hearted yet strong,
considerate and full of
compassion - a rare and
valuable presence aboard
the Iron Gear, where so
many others have fiery
tempers.
 Skilled with firearms, he
handles every job
imaginable: piloting and
maintaining Walker
Machines, and serving as
both helmsman and gunner
aboard the Iron Gear.
Despite all this, he never
once got a moment in the
spotlight - a fact
summed up perfectly by
his own line, "That's
because I'm a side
character." He seems to
understand his own role
perfectly well, which may
make him the most
emotionally mature person
in the entire cast.

A member of the bandit
gang Sand Rat.
 She carries a little
bear-shaped pouch and

her work with real
professional skill. She
often rides along with
Jiron in the Xabungle or
Walker Gallier to provide
support.
 Her sharp remarks about
other people's psychology
hint at real depth of
insight and a maturity
beyond her years. Even
so, she cries and screams
like any child her age
when things get
dangerous.
 In Jiron's words, she
will "grow up to be quite
a woman."

Chill is a member of the
Sand Rat bandit group.
She carries a bear-shaped
pouch and serves as
something of a mascot,
but she performs her
work professionally and
without fail. Her remarks
sharply pointing out the
psychology of others
reveal her deep insight
and mature mental age.
Still, when she cries out
in moments of peril, she
seems every bit her age.
According to Jiron, she
will 'grow into a fine
woman someday'.

A member of the Iron
Gear crew. Age 15.
 She was once a member
of the anti-Innocent
organization 'Salt,' but
gave up on their leader
Katakam out of
frustration with his
ineffectiveness, and,
agreeing with Jiron's
views, ended up where she
is now.
 Her active personality
suits her for
reconnaissance and
intelligence work using a
small Walker Machine
called the Leg, which she
carried out energetically.
 She and Maria have
fought together aboard a
captured Doran, and the
two seem to get along
well in general, including
forming the self-styled
'Arthur Honor Guard'
together and generally
having fun.

A girl who gathered
orphans together and ran
a self-sufficient farm.
 A thoroughgoing pacifist.
Taking care of others is
considered eccentric
behavior on Zora, and Rag
did in fact call her a
strange one. After
meeting Jiron and
recognizing her own
naivety, she cut off her
long hair as a way of
atoning for it.
 She later joined 'Salt'
as an assistant to Medic.
After reuniting with Jiron
and the others, she began
taking up a gun herself
and joining the fighting.
 After Arthur's
appearance, she became a
huge fan of his along
with Rag and Birin,
squealing with excitement
over him like any ordinary
girl.

A wandering Civilian
doctor.
 A heavy drinker, but a
reliable physician. At the
outset he treated Jiron's
arm and even gave him
clothes, only to have the
payment for it stolen by
Rag, effectively leaving
him stiffed for his
trouble.
 He later passed through
'Salt' before coming
aboard the Iron Gear,
where he served
afterward as Jiron's
strategic advisor. He is a
man of considerable
intelligence, at times
making remarks that seem
to see straight through
the Innocents' intentions.

The Breaker who killed
Jiron's parents. He seemed
at first to be a mere
drifter, but he is in fact
an agent of the
Innocents, whose job is
to pit Civilians against
each other under the
guise of 'trials.'
 His cunning, his skill
piloting Walker Machines,
and his quick-draw
marksmanship are all
first-rate, and his
manner carries the air of
a truly formidable figure.
Yet he has a slightly
bumbling side too, and
provided plenty of comic
moments, such as burning
his nose on the cigar
clenched in his teeth.
 He fought Jiron again
and again as Jiron
pursued him to avenge his
parents, and when it
finally seemed he had
been defeated, he once
got himself out of danger
by playing dead.

Timmp Sharon is the
breaker who killed Jiron's
parents. He seemed to be
a drifter, but in truth
he was an agent of the
Innocent, who instigate
battles between civilians
under the guise of trials.
His cunning, his mastery
of Walker Machine
piloting, and his quick
draw with a gun are all
top-notch, and his
bearing carries the air of
a true big shot. Yet
there is a certain
absent-mindedness about
him, and he provided many
comical moments, such as
burning his nose with the
cigar he kept in his
mouth. He fought fierce
battles time and again
against Jiron, who pursued
him for revenge, and when
he finally seemed to have
been defeated at Jiron's
hands, he once managed
to survive the crisis by
playing dead. In the end,
he survived to the very
last, and he was still in
fine form in the final
scene.

A Breaker acting as an
agent of the Innocents.
 He was once the leader
of the Breakers employed
by Carrying Cargo, but
Jiron's arrival threw
everything into chaos and
cost him his position.
 From then on he devoted
himself entirely to
scheming toward two
goals: defeating Jiron,
and winning over Elchi,
whose affections he
continued to pursue
despite her rejection.
 When he first appeared
he came across as
cool-headed and sharp,
but he grew increasingly
sloppy as time went on.
By the latter half of the
story, it had become a
running gag for him to
take his failures out on
his partner Geraba.

Kid Hola is a breaker
who works as an agent of
the Innocent. He was
formerly the leader of
the breakers employed by
Cargo, but the arrival of
Jiron threw everything
into chaos and cost him
that position. From then
on, he constantly schemed
to achieve two goals: to
defeat Jiron, and to win
the heart of Elchi, who
had rejected him but
whom he continued to
love. At first he gave
the impression of a calm
and collected sharp
operator, but gradually
his sloppiness became
more and more apparent.
In the latter half, his
trademark became taking
out his frustrations on
his partner Geraba
whenever he failed.
Though he had no part to
play in the final battle,
he appeared properly in
the last scene, making
sure to show that he was
still going strong.

Hola's subordinate,
partner, and little
brother figure.
 Tough-looking and strong
in a fight, he is also no
slouch at piloting Walker
Machines. Surprisingly
timid at heart, though, he
cannot bring himself to
defy Hola, having been
beaten by him once
before.
 He once pulled off the
bold feat of infiltrating
the Iron Gear by
pretending to have given
up on Hola, then
kidnapping Elchi. The
acting skill he showed off
in the process makes one
wonder whether he could
not, in fact, stand on his
own without Hola.

Subordinate, partner, and
junior to Hola. Despite
his intimidating
appearance and physical
strength, and his skill at
piloting Walker Machines,
he is surprisingly timid
and cannot defy Hola, who
once defeated him. He
pulled off the bold move
of infiltrating the Iron
Gear while pretending to
abandon Hola, and
abducting Elchi. His acting
ability on that occasion
makes one cannot help
but think he could stand
on his own even without
teaming up with Hola. He
had no part in the final
battle, but his appearance
at the very end was,
indeed, just like Hola.

Wife of the courier
Karasu Karasu.
 The sex appeal radiating
from her overly
voluptuous figure is
intense enough to
overwhelm even Jiron, and
more than a few Breakers
have fallen prey to her
deep, lingering thank-you
kisses.
 When she was shot down
during an attack on the
Iron Gear, her husband,
believing her dead,
launched a war of
vengeance - only to be
beaten back himself.
Through this convoluted
turn of events, she ended
up being the one avenging
her husband instead, and
has relentlessly pursued
the Iron Gear ever since.

Wife of the transporter
Karas Karas. Her charm,
emanating from her overly
voluptuous figure, was so
powerful that even Jiron
was overwhelmed, and not
a few Breakers fell victim
to the passionate kiss
she gave as a token of
gratitude. When she was
shot down during the
attack on the Iron Gear,
Karas believed her dead
and launched a revenge
battle, but was instead
defeated. This led to the
complicated turn of
events where she herself
now sought to avenge her
husband, and thereafter
she persistently targeted
the Iron Gear. In the
end, following the advice
of Elchi, freed from
mental control, she
resolved to live on to
find new love.

The supreme ruler of
the Innocents. Age 17. His
name is a hereditary
title, not his actual birth
name.
 Betrayed by his close
aide Cashim, he was
imprisoned at Yopp Point
until Jiron and the others
rescued him. He then
declared to all the
Innocents that Cashim
must be overthrown.
 Innocents cannot survive
for long in the open air,
and it is this frailty,
along with his innocent
nature and above all his
beauty, that has
captivated Rag, Birin, and
Maria.

The supreme authority
of the Innocent. He is 17
years old. The name is
hereditary, not his real
name. Betrayed by his
aide Kashim, he was
imprisoned at Yop Point
until rescued by Jiron and
the others. Afterwards,
he declared to all the
Innocent that he would
overthrow Kashim. The
Innocent cannot survive
long in outside air, and
his resulting frailty, his
innocent personality, and
above all his beauty made
Rag, Birin, and Maria
smitten with him. When
Elchi suffered from
Kashim's personality being
transplanted into her, he
ordered that it be
transferred into his own
body to save her. And
when he realized he could
not suppress the Kashim
within, he took his own
life. However, at the end
of the theatrical version,
for some reason he
appears healthy and
lively, exciting the women
greatly.

A Newtype boy who joins
the AEUG, and the pilot
of the Zeta Gundam. He
is 17 years old.
 Originally an ordinary, if
somewhat sensitive, high
school student on the
space colony 'Green Noa.'
He has a complex about
his feminine-sounding
name, Kamille, which led
him to throw himself into
more masculine hobbies
like the Homo Avis (a
simple hang glider) and
karate. Perhaps thanks to
having parents who were
technical officers in the
Federation Forces, he is
also well versed in
machinery himself, skilled
enough to win the Jr.
Mobile Suit tournament.
 When Jerid mocked his
name and the two came to
blows, however, he found
himself at odds with the
Titans. Circumstances led
him to help Quattro steal
the Gundam Mk-II, and he
ended up joining the AEUG
outright. Through combat
he awakened to his
abilities as a Newtype,
and gradually rose to
become one of the AEUG's
ace pilots.
 At first he simply
fought out of resentment
toward the Titans, but
through his encounters
and partings with adults
like Quattro and Amuro,
and with women like Four
and Rosamia, he grew
tremendously as a person.
In time, while searching
for a way to end the
war, he came to fly
through space guided by
his own will.

the AEUG, and pilot of
the Zeta Gundam. He is
17. Originally an ordinary,

attending high school in

Noa. He had a complex
about his feminine name
Kamille, and leaned toward
masculine hobbies such as
Homo Avis (simple
gliders) and karate.

parents being Federation

name and he got into a

into conflict with the
Titans. He ended up
helping Quattro's plan to
seize the Gundam Mk-II,
and joined the AEUG as a
result. In battle, his
Newtype abilities
awakened, and he
gradually came to be
active as an ace pilot of
the AEUG. Initially
fighting simply out of
resentment toward the
Titans, he grew greatly
as a person through his
encounters and partings
with adults such as
Quattro and Amuro, and
women such as Four and
Rosamia. And while seeking
a way to end the war, he
came to race through
space by his own will. At
the end of the TV
version, his spirit was
dragged down by Scirocco,
leaving deep wounds on
his heart. But at the end
of the theatrical version,
he cast that aside and
confirmed each other's
safety with Fa.

One of the central
figures who laid the
foundations of the AEUG.
His rank is captain. He is
27 years old.
 A man of many
mysteries, who wears
sunglasses that hide his
true face. His true
identity is Char Aznable,
the Red Comet of the
Principality of Zeon
forces, who went missing
after the end of the One
Year War.
 Incidentally, Quattro is
Italian for the number
'4', marking it as the
fourth name he has used
- after his birth name,
Casval, his Earth alias,
Edwau, and his Zeon alias,
Char.
 At first he made use of
his outstanding mobile
suit piloting skill,
fighting on the front
lines aboard the Rick Dias
and the Hyaku Shiki. But
his reunion with Amuro,
along with the
assassination of Brigadier
General Blex, the AEUG's
representative, led him to
step into the spotlight
as a political leader.

One of the central
figures who built the
foundation of the AEUG.
His rank is captain. He is
27. A mysterious man who
wears sunglasses that
conceal his true face. His
true identity is Char
Aznable, the Red Comet of
the Principality of Zeon,
who went missing after
the end of the One Year
War. Incidentally,
'Quattro' is the Italian
word for the number 4,
meaning it is his fourth
name, following his real
name Casval, his alias on
Earth Edwou, and his alias
in the Principality of
Zeon, Char. At first, he
used his high mobile suit
piloting skills to fight on
the front lines in a Rick
Dias and the Hyaku Shiki.
But his reunion with
Amuro and the
assassination of AEUG
chairperson Blex, among
other things, led him to
stand on the political
stage as a leader. In the
final phase, he engaged in
a one-on-one duel with
Haman on the stage of
the Colony Laser, but due
to the performance
difference between the
mobile suits, his machine
was wrecked. He vanished
into the explosion, and
went missing once again.

The ace pilot of Karaba.
His rank is captain. He is
24 years old.
 A man who fought
through the One Year War
in the RX-78 Gundam and
has since become
something of a legend.
After the war, however,
he came to be seen as a
threat and was kept
under Federation
surveillance, left to
languish in an unimportant
post on Earth. By this
time he had lost nearly
all his will to fight -
partly due to the
oppressive environment,
but mostly because of
the trauma left by his
encounter and parting
with Lalah Sune.
 A sudden visit from
Fraw, Katz, and their
family, however, prompted
him to resolve to stand
up and fight again. After
deserting and joining up
with Karaba, he began
working alongside his old
rival Char and the
youthful Kamille. As the
fighting continued, he
regained his old instincts,
and, piloting the Rick
Dias and later the Dijeh,
became a core fighting
force for Karaba.

Captain of the AEUG
cruiser Argama. His rank
is lieutenant colonel.
 During the One Year
War, though only an
officer cadet,
circumstances placed him
in command of the White
Base, which he saw
through to the end of
the war. His distinguished
performance, however,
made him a figure the top
brass viewed with
suspicion, and after the
war he was shunted into
the unimportant post of
captain of the liaison
shuttle 'Temptation.'
 Harboring doubts about
the self-righteous
methods of the Titans, he
accepted Quattro's
invitation and decided to
join the AEUG.
 Drawing on the
experience he built up
during the One Year War,
his sound command has led
to numerous victories.
