A bridge crewman of the
Argama, serving with the
AEUG.
 A cheerful, easygoing
sort. His main duties are
the ship's navigation,
communications, and
sensor tracking, and he
gets along well with
Saegusa, who sits next to
him and handles much the
same role.
 In the TV version he
often hung around with
Kamille as well, and once
teased him into a fight
that got him sent to
detention.

A bridge crew member of
the Argama who has
joined the AEUG. He is a
cheerful and easygoing
character. His main role
is the ship's navigation
and
communications/sensor
operations, and he is on
good terms with Saegusa,
whose seat is next to his
and who performs nearly
the same duties. In the
TV version, he once got
into a fight with Kamille
after teasing him and was
ordered to go to the
study room.

A bridge crewman of the
Argama.
 His main duties are the
ship's navigation and
helm, and he gets along
well with Torres, who sits
next to him and handles
much the same role.

A bridge crew member of
the Argama. His main role
is the ship's navigation
and steering. He is on
good terms with Torres,
whose seat is next to his
and who performs nearly
the same duties. At the
end of the theatrical
version, he was still
handling navigation during
the quiet conversation in
which Kamille and Fa
confirmed each other's
presence.

Once a member of the
Titans, she defected to
the AEUG after witnessing
Basque's despicable
tactics firsthand. Her
rank remains lieutenant.
 Her outstanding piloting
skill was apparently
valued in the AEUG as
well, and she was
entrusted with mainstay
machines such as the Rick
Dias, the Gundam Mk-II,
and the Super Gundam, all
of which she handled with
ease.
 She has a strong will
that acts on her own
convictions, along with
the sternness of a
soldier. At the same time,
she also carries a
feminine gentleness. She
always kept up a cold
front toward Henken's
advances, but in truth
she does not seem to
have minded them all that
much.

Originally a member of
the Titans, she defected
to the AEUG after
witnessing Basque's
despicable tactics. Her
rank remained lieutenant.
Her high piloting skill was
evidently valued within
the AEUG, as she was
entrusted with main units
such as the Rick Dias,
the Gundam Mk-II, and
the Super Gundam, and
she handled them
skillfully. She possessed
strong will, acting on her
own convictions, along
with a soldier's
strictness. Yet at the
same time, she also had a
feminine gentleness.
Though she always gave
Henken a cold shoulder in
response to his advances,
in truth she was not
entirely indifferent to
him. In the final battle
against the Titans, after
Reccoa was shot down,
she exited her immobilized
mobile suit and was
struck across the body
by debris fragments from
Yazan's bombardment.
Afterward, entrusting her
final words to Kamille,
who rushed to her side,
she passed away in his
arms.

An officer of the
Titans. Her rank is
lieutenant. She is 24
years old.
 Her mobile suit piloting
skill is high enough that
she was selected as a
pilot for the Gundam
Mk-II despite being a
woman.
 Amid the many Titans
who hold to an elitist,
chosen-people ideology,
she is one of the few
with any real sense of
decency, and this leads
her to feel disgust at
Basque's ruthless,
by-any-means tactics.

An officer of the
Titans. Her rank is
lieutenant. She is 24
years old.
 Her mobile suit piloting
skill is high enough that
she was selected as a
pilot for the Gundam
Mk-II despite being a
woman.
 Amid the many Titans
who hold to an elitist,
chosen-people ideology,
she is one of the few
with any real sense of
decency, and this leads
her to feel disgust at
Basque's ruthless,
by-any-means tactics.

A member of the AEUG,
with the rank of ensign.
She is 23 years old.
 She lost her parents
during the One Year War
and spent time taking
part in guerrilla activity
in North America. Having
grown up amid fighting,
she is a brave soldier
who readily volunteers
even for spy missions
with death constantly at
hand. At the same time,
though, she longed for a
man who could be a
source of emotional
support.

A member of the AEUG,
with the rank of ensign.
She is 23 years old.
 She lost her parents
during the One Year War
and spent time taking
part in guerrilla activity
in North America. Having
grown up amid fighting,
she is a brave soldier
who readily volunteers
even for spy missions
with death constantly at
hand. At the same time,
though, she longed for a
man who could be a
source of emotional
support.

A former member of the
AEUG, now an officer of
the Titans. Her rank is
ensign.
 She sought comfort in
Quattro, but his attitude
and words made her
realize she was not
needed by him, leaving her
disillusioned. While on a
mission she then met
Scirocco, and, drawn to
him, defected to the
Titans.
 From that point on she
no longer carried out spy
work as she had with the
AEUG, devoting herself
instead to piloting the
Pallas Athene.

A former member of the
AEUG, now an officer in
the Titans with the rank
of ensign. She sought
solace in Quattro, but his
attitude and words made
her realize she was not
needed, and she despaired.
Then she met Scirocco
during a mission, was
drawn to him, and
defected to the Titans.
From then on, she ceased
the spy activities she
had conducted during her
AEUG days and devoted
herself to piloting the
Palas Athena. During the
final battle, she fought
Emma, who was also a
turncoat but on the
opposite side. She heavily
damaged the Gundam Mk-II
but had her own mobile
suit shot down, and she
perished hating men to
the very end.

A subordinate of
Quattro's who joins the
AEUG. His rank is
lieutenant.
 He formerly belonged to
the old Principality of
Zeon forces and took
part in the One Year War
as well. He is one of the
few veteran pilots aboard
the Argama, and a good
senior figure to Kamille.
 He is deeply trusted by
Quattro, and has at times
taken command of the
mobile suit corps in his
place.

A subordinate of
Quattro who joined the
AEUG. His rank was
lieutenant. He had
originally served in the
Principality of Zeon and
had participated in the
One Year War. He was one
of the few veteran pilots
aboard the Argama and
was a good senior to
Kamille. Quattro placed
great trust in him, and
at times he led the
mobile suit team in
Quattro's place. In both
the TV series and the
theatrical version, he
died shielding Fa's
Methuss.

A subordinate of
Quattro's who joins the
AEUG. His rank is
lieutenant.
 He formerly belonged to
the old Principality of
Zeon forces and took
part in the One Year War
as well. He is one of the
few veteran pilots aboard
the Argama, and a good
senior figure to Kamille.
 He and Apolly are
comrades who have
survived countless brushes
with death together, and
the two are often found
acting side by side.

Roberto is a subordinate
of Quattro in the
Anti-Earth Union Group,
holding the rank of
Lieutenant. He formerly
served in the Principality
of Zeon and participated
in the One Year War. He
is one of the few
veteran pilots aboard the
Argama and served as a
good senior to Kamille. He
and Apolly are comrades
who have faced countless
life-and-death situations
together, and they often
act in tandem. In the
television version, he is
shot down and killed by
Buran's Asshimar while
escorting the shuttle
that the AEUG pilots use
to ascend to space.
However, in the theatrical
version, he simply
disappears without a
specific death scene.
Although the possibility
of survival remains,
compared to his partner
who even received a
surname, he seems to
have been rather
shortchanged by the
theatrical adaptation.

Kamille's childhood
friend, age 17. Her name,
written in kanji, would be
'Hanazono Rei.'
 Because she was known
to be an acquaintance of
Kamille, who stole the
Gundam Mk-II, she and
her parents were captured
by Basque. After Bright
rescued her, she joined
the AEUG - partly out of
defiance toward the
Titans - and volunteered
as a pilot. Though
troubled by her own lack
of skill, she fought her
way through the entire
Gryps War.
 She has a fussy,
caretaking personality and
has long kept after
Kamille about his everyday
habits and manners.
Kamille, for his part,
seems to have found her
nagging rather tiresome
deep down. Perhaps
because of her
personality, she also
became the one
responsible for looking
after Shinta and Kum, the
children Quattro brought
aboard the Argama.

Fa is Kamille's childhood
friend and is seventeen
years old. Her name, when
written in kanji, is
'Hanazono Rei'. Because
she was an acquaintance
of Kamille, who stole the
Gundam Mk-II, she was
captured along with her
parents by Basque. After
being rescued by Bright,
she joined the AEUG out
of defiance toward the
Titans and volunteered as
a pilot. While struggling
with her own lack of
skill, she fought through
the Gryps Conflict. She
has a nurturing
personality and has long
admonished Kamille about
his lifestyle and habits.
Kamille apparently found
her nagging inwardly
tiresome. Perhaps because
of this nature, she also
became the caretaker for
Shinta and Kum, whom
Quattro brought aboard
the Argama. In the
television version, because
her beloved Kamille lost
his sanity in the final
battle, she later left the
battlefield to devote
herself to his care and
nursing. In the theatrical
version, however, the two
finished the war with
their bodies intact, and
they were seen rejoicing
over each other's safety.

A boy soldier who joins
the AEUG.
 Having come aboard the
White Base as a refugee
during the One Year War,
he was raised after the
war as the adopted son
of Hayato and Fraw. When
the family visited Amuro,
however, he volunteered
on his own to join the
AEUG, and joined up with
Amuro aboard the
Audomura.
 A complete change from
his quiet childhood self,
he has grown into a
reckless, hot-blooded
young man. He harbors
rivalry toward Kamille,
who is close to him in
age, and shows a boyish
immaturity - launching
without authorization,
ignoring orders, and
falling for Sara, whom he
met on the battlefield.

Katz is a boy soldier
who joins the AEUG.
During the One Year War,
because of his connection
to boarding the White
Base as a refugee, he
was raised after the war
as the adopted son of
Hayato and Fraw's family.
However, when his family
visited Amuro, he
volunteered on his own to
join the AEUG and
rendezvoused with Amuro
aboard the Audhumla. In
contrast to his quiet
childhood, he became
reckless and hot-blooded.
He held a rival
consciousness toward
Kamille, who was the same
age, and sometimes
sortied without permission
or ignored orders. He fell
in love with Sara, a
subordinate of Scirocco,
whom he met on the
battlefield, and tried to
persuade her to leave his
side. But his words were
rejected, and worse, he
ended up killing her with
his own beam. In the
final battle against the
Titans, he performed a
feat of saving Emma from
a desperate situation.
However, while fleeing
from Yazan's grasp, he
collided with an asteroid
and scattered his young
life in space.

An officer of the
Titans, with the rank of
lieutenant. He is 24 years
old.
 Highly elitist by nature,
he secretly harbors
ambitions of seizing
control of the Titans.
 Selected as a pilot for
the Gundam Mk-II
alongside Kacricon and
Emma, he had been
enjoying smooth sailing as
a soldier's career. His
encounter with Kamille,
however, threw his fate
badly off course.
 At first he was
unfamiliar with mobile suit
piloting, crash-landing the
Gundam Mk-II and
standing no chance at all
against Quattro. But
fueled in part by his
personal grudge against
Kamille, he steadily
improved, gradually
drawing the attention of
both Jamitov and Scirocco.
He then went through one
new machine after another
- the Marasai, the
Gabthley, the Byarlant,
the Baund Doc -
relentlessly pursuing
Kamille all the while.

Jerid is an officer in
the Titans with the rank
of Lieutenant and is
twenty-four years old. He
has a strong sense of
elitism and harbors a
hidden ambition to seize
control of the Titans. He
had been walking a smooth
path as a soldier, having
been selected along with
Kacricon and Emma as
pilots of the Gundam
Mk-II. However, his fate
was thrown severely off
course by his encounter
with Kamille. Initially, he
was unfamiliar with
handling mobile suits,
having crash-landed the
Gundam Mk-II and being
unable to do anything
against Quattro. Yet,
perhaps driven by his
personal grudge against
Kamille, he steadily
improved and gradually
began to catch the
attention of Jamitov and
Scirocco. While losing
close people one after
another - Lila, Kacricon,
and Mouar - he kept
switching to new machines
such as the Marasai,
Gabthley, Byarlant, and
Baund Doc, relentlessly
pursuing Kamille. However,
even at the end, he was
outmatched, and after his
machine was shot through,
he was swallowed by the
explosion of the Radish.
What he attempted to say
at the end remains an
eternal mystery.

An officer of the
Titans, with the rank of
lieutenant. He is 24 years
old.
 He was selected as a
pilot for the Gundam
Mk-II alongside Jerid and
Emma. He gets along well
with his colleague Jerid
and the two are nearly
always together.
 Besides being a skilled
mobile suit pilot, he is
also sharp-minded, the
scheming, strategist type.
 He apparently had a
girlfriend on Earth named
Amelia.

Kacricon is an officer in
the Titans with the rank
of Lieutenant and is
twenty-four years old. He
was selected along with
Jerid and Emma as a pilot
of the Gundam Mk-II. He
got along well with his
colleague Jerid and always
acted with him. He is not
only skilled at piloting
mobile suits but is also a
keen strategist with a
sharp mind. He apparently
had a lover on Earth
named Amelia, and when
his Varute was slashed
open by Kamille's Gundam
Mk-II during atmospheric
entry, he shouted her
name from within the
burning wreckage, and
those were his final
words.

A pilot of the Galbady
Beta assigned to the
Titans cruiser 'Bosnie.'
Her rank is captain.
 Despite being a woman,
her piloting skill is such
that she commands the
Galbady squadron.
Blunt-spoken and
combative by nature, she
made no effort to hide
her rivalry with the
blatantly elitist Jerid,
dismissing him outright as
a "soft little boy."

Lila Mira Raira was a
pilot of a Galbady Beta
assigned to the Titans
cruiser Bosnia, with the
rank of Lieutenant.
 Despite being a woman,
she possessed piloting
skill enough to serve as
the leader of the Galbady
unit. With her blunt
speech and combative
personality, she made no
effort to hide her rivalry
toward Jerid, whose
elitist attitude she
dismissed by calling him a
'spoiled little boy.'
 In the battle against
the AEUG as they
attempted to descend to
Jaburo, she engaged
Kamille's Gundam Mk-II.
She was shot down
without being able to lay
a hand on Kamille, who
had only recently begun
piloting a mobile suit.
 Unlike the TV version,
where she saw potential
in Jerid to become a fine
man, her role was greatly
altered in the theatrical
version. In the battle
against Scirocco, she
appeared among the
figures floating around
Kamille, but...

A member of the Titans
who serves as both
captain of the Garuda and
pilot of the Asshimar. His
rank is major.
 Excellent both as a
commander and a pilot, he
is deeply trusted by his
subordinates. His
arrogant, overbearing
manner is simply the
expression of a
confidence backed by real
ability.
 He detests the
instability of Enhanced
Humans, and seems to
have found the newly
assigned Rosamia an
unwelcome presence as
well.
 Tasked with hunting
down the Audomura, he
pursued Kamille and the
others relentlessly, time
after time.

Bran Bulltaak was a
member of the Titans who
served concurrently as
the captain of the Garuda
and the pilot of an
Asshimar, with the rank
of Major.
 He was excellent both as
a commander and as a
pilot, and enjoyed the
strong trust of his
subordinates. His arrogant
and haughty demeanor was
a reflection of confidence
backed by real ability.
 He detested the
instability of enhanced
humans and reportedly
viewed Rosamia, who had
been assigned to his unit,
with distaste.
 Tasked with the mission
to eliminate the Audhumla,
he pursued Kamille and
the others on numerous
occasions.
 He fought Kamille and
Quattro simultaneously
and showed his high skill,
more than holding his own
against them. In the end,
however, he was defeated
by the combined efforts
of Amuro and Kamille.

Bran's adjutant, who
takes command of the
Garuda's combat
operations whenever Bran
sorties.
 After Bran's death, he
took over as captain of
the Garuda and tried to
avenge Bran using Four's
Psycho Gundam, though he
seems to have remained
skeptical of the very
existence of Enhanced
Humans.

Ben Woodder was Bran's
adjutant, and when Bran
sortied, he took command
of combat operations
aboard the Garuda.
 After Bran's death, he
assumed the captaincy of
the Garuda and attempted
to avenge Bran using
Four's Psycho Gundam.
However, he appeared to
be skeptical of the very
existence of enhanced
humans.
 After the battle in Hong
Kong, he finally resolved
to carry out a suicide
attack against the
Audhumla using a
Garuda-class ship. He
issued an order for the
crew to abandon ship, but
the fact that some
remained despite the
order suggests he was
deeply trusted by his
subordinates.

Rosamia was a
cyber-newtype trained at
the Augusta Research
Institute, holding the
nominal rank of
lieutenant. She lost her
family in a colony drop
during the One Year War,
and her trauma was
exploited for mental
enhancement. However, the
repeated experiments and
enhancements caused her
mind to become unstable.
She was assigned to
Bran's unit and fought
Kamille numerous times in
her Gaplant.

Rosamia Badam was an
enhanced human trained at
the Augusta Research
Institute, with the
nominal rank of Second
Lieutenant.
 She had lost her family
in the colony drop during
the One Year War, and
that trauma was exploited
to perform mental
reinforcement on her.
However, the repeated
experiments and the side
effects of the
enhancement left her mind
unstable.
 She was incorporated
into Bran's unit and
frequently engaged Kamille
in her Gaplant.
 In the TV version, she
was implanted with false
memories of being
Kamille's sister, but
ultimately suffered a
mental breakdown and died
at Kamille's hands. In the
theatrical version,
however, after being shot
down at Hickory, she had
no explicit death scene
and appeared as a spirit
in the finale, bearing
part of the Zeta
Gundam's power.

Four was a
cyber-newtype trained at
the Murasame Research
Institute and the pilot of
the Psyco Gundam, holding
the nominal rank of
lieutenant. Ordinarily
gentle and mild-mannered,
when she boarded the
Psyco Gundam she came
under the influence of
its mental control waves,
transforming into a
violent personality
accompanied by intense
headaches. She had lost
her memories of the past,
and this deep-seated
complex bound her tightly.
The name Four was not
her real name; it merely
marked her as the fourth
test subject at the
Murasame Institute. Yet
she believed the words
that destroying the
Gundam Mk-II would
restore her memories, and
endured her headaches to
remain in the Psyco
Gundam's cockpit. Meeting
Kamille let her touch the
warmth of the human
heart, but learning that
he was the Gundam
Mk-II's pilot brought her
great anguish.

Four Murasame was an
enhanced human trained at
the Murasame Research
Institute and the pilot of
the Psycho Gundam, with
the nominal rank of
Second Lieutenant.
 Ordinarily gentle and
mild-mannered, when she
boarded the Psycho
Gundam she came under
the influence of its
mental control waves,
transforming into a
violent personality
accompanied by intense
headaches.
 She had lost her
memories of the past, and
that loss was a deep
complex that bound her
tightly. The name Four
was not her real name;
it merely meant she was
the fourth test subject
at the Murasame
Institute. Yet she
believed the words that
defeating the Gundam
Mk-II would restore her
memories, and endured her
headaches to keep sitting
in the Psycho Gundam's
cockpit.
 Through meeting Kamille,
she came into contact
with the warmth of the
human heart, but upon
learning he was the
Gundam Mk-II pilot, she
fell into anguish.
 In both the TV and
theatrical versions, she
lost her life amid the
flames of war. In either
case, it was the result
of throwing herself into
danger for Kamille's sake,
breaking free of her
shackles, so perhaps it
was her true wish.

Mauar was a Titans
officer of seventeen,
holding the rank of
lieutenant. She met Jerid
while escaping from
Jaburo, and as they
worked together she came
to love him and his
abilities. She possessed
solid piloting skill backed
by calm judgment and
initiative. Scirocco
recognized her potential,
but she saw him as a
danger and refused his
offer. She continued to
support Jerid unwaveringly
as he burned to defeat
Kamille.

Mauer Pharao was an
officer of the Titans
with the rank of junior
lieutenant. She met Jerid
while escaping from
Jaburo, and as they began
to work together, she
came to love both him
and his abilities. Her
piloting skill was solid,
backed by calm judgment
and decisive action. Her
talent was noticed by
Scirocco, but she refused
his offer, as she saw him
as a danger. She
continued to support
Jerid, who burned with
the desire to defeat
Kamille, and died
protecting him from an
attack by the Zeta
Gundam.

Yazan was a Titans
officer, initially a
lieutenant and later
promoted to captain. He
had a belligerent
personality and genuinely
enjoyed war, where he
could wield his strength
freely. As a pilot he
showed exceptional skill,
handling high-mobility
mobile suits such as the
Gaplant and Hambrabi like
extensions of his own
body, and repeatedly
harried the Argama's
mobile suit team. He
possessed the cunning and
cruelty to murder even a
superior officer without
hesitation if it suited
his purposes. Yet he also
had a caring side, and
seemed to be trusted
deeply by subordinates
such as Ramsus and
Dunkel.

Yazan Gable was an
officer of the Titans. His
initial rank was
lieutenant, but he was
later promoted to captain.
He had a belligerent
personality and truly
enjoyed war, where he
could wield his own power
freely. As a pilot, he
displayed exceptional
skill, maneuvering
high-mobility mobile suits
such as the Gaplant and
Hambrabi as if they were
extensions of his own
body, and he repeatedly
troubled the mobile suit
team of the Argama. He
possessed the cunning and
cruelty to murder even
his superiors without
hesitation if it was
inconvenient for him.
However, he also had a
caring side, and he
seemed to be trusted
deeply by his
subordinates, including
Rumsas and Dunkel. His
wickedness, which
culminated in taking the
lives of Katz and Emma
and even laughing aloud,
triggered the activation
of the biosensor in
Kamille's Zeta Gundam. His
machine was destroyed by
overwhelming power, and
he barely escaped, but he
was left adrift in space.

Dunkel was a Titans
officer and a member of
the Hambrabi squadron
commanded by Yazan. His
skill as a pilot was solid,
and through coordinated
attacks he troubled the
Argama on numerous
occasions.

Dunkel Cooper was an
officer of the Titans and
a member of the Hambrabi
unit commanded by Yazan.
His skill as a pilot was
solid, and through
coordinated attacks he
troubled the Argama on
numerous occasions, but
in the final phase of the
war he was shot down and
killed by Kamille's Zeta
Gundam.

Ramsus Hasa was an
officer of the Titans and
a member of the Hambrabi
unit commanded by Yazan.
Though coarse in
personality, he possessed
solid skill as a pilot.
This can be seen from
the fact that Yazan
trusted him enough to
recruit him as a
subordinate and entrust
him with a new model
mobile suit.
 His rough nature did not
hinder his competence,
and his reliability in
battle made him a valued
asset within the unit.

Rumsas Hasa was an
officer of the Titans and
a member of the Hambrabi
unit commanded by Yazan.
Though he had a rough
personality, his skill as a
pilot was genuine. This
can be seen from the
fact that even Yazan
trusted him enough to
recruit him as a
subordinate and provide
him with a new mobile
suit. He persistently
pursued the Argama, but
in the final phase of the
Gryps War, he was shot
down and killed along with
Dunkel by Emma's Gundam
Mk-II.

Sara Zabirov was a
Newtype candidate of the
Titans. Her rank was
sergeant. She was drawn
to Scirocco, who
acknowledged her, and
swore absolute loyalty to
him. Though the words of
Kamille and Katz moved
her heart, she never left
his side.
 Her devotion remained
unwavering even as she
wrestled with the doubts
they planted in her mind.

Sara Zabirov was a
Newtype candidate of the
Titans with the rank of
sergeant. She was drawn
to Scirocco, who
recognized her worth, and
swore absolute loyalty to
him. Though the words of
Kamille and Katz moved
her heart, she never left
his side. In the
three-way battle among
the AEUG, the Titans, and
Axis, she died when she
intercepted with her own
mobile suit a beam that
Katz had fired at
Scirocco. In the
theatrical version, her
spirit afterward protected
Katz from an enraged
Scirocco, suggesting that
her feelings for Katz had
swayed her considerably.

Paptimus Scirocco was
the captain of the
Jupiter ship Jupitris,
leading the Jupiter fleet
of the Earth Federation
government. His rank was
lieutenant commander. He
was 26 years old. He
possessed high Newtype
abilities and charisma.
Furthermore, he was a
genius who perfectly
handled everything from
mobile suit design to
piloting, operational
planning and command, and
even the handling of
women. This power
charmed Sara, caused
Reccoa to defect from
the AEUG, and even
brought the highly
selective Yazan over to
his side.
 He openly stated that
'after the war, women will
rule the world,' but the
meaning of these words
remained unclear to the
end. After returning to
the Earth sphere, he
belonged to the Titans,
but the ambition born of
his talent seemed not to
fit within the framework
of the military.

Papetimus Scirocco,
captain of the Jupiter
fleet ship Jupitris under
the Earth Federation
government, held the rank
of lieutenant and was 26
years old. Possessing high
Newtype ability and
charisma, he was a genius
who could perfectly
handle everything from
mobile suit design to
piloting, strategy planning
and command, to the
handling of women. His
power captivated Sara,
caused Reccoa to defect
from the Anti-Earth Union
Group, and even drew the
notoriously picky Yazan
to his side. He openly
stated that 'after the
war, women will rule the
world,' but the true
meaning of those words
remained unclear until the
end. After returning to
the Earth Sphere, he
joined the Titans, but
the ambition born of his
talent could not be
contained within the
framework of the military,
and he seized control of
the Titans by
assassinating Jamitov amid
the confusion. In the end,
he boarded the Zeta
Gundam's rival, The O,
which he had designed
himself, and engaged in a
fierce battle with Kamille.
However, before the power
of the souls surrounding
Kamille, he was utterly
defeated.

Basque Om was the
right-hand man of
Jamitov, who founded the
Titans, and was in effect
the supreme commander of
military operations. His
rank was colonel. He was
37 years old. To
compensate for his
weakened eyesight, he
always wore goggles like
underwater swimming
glasses. It was said this
came from the
aftereffects of torture
suffered when he was
captured by the
Principality of Zeon
forces during the One
Year War.
 He had a cruel
personality that showed
no mercy to anyone other
than the Titans,
especially Spacenoids. He
would not hesitate to use
poison gas against
colonies or take hostages
to recover the Gundam
Mk-II, choosing any means
to achieve his goals. He
was truly a man who
symbolized the Titans.

Basque Om was the
trusted subordinate of
Jamitov, founder of the
Titans, and effectively
the supreme military
commander, holding the
rank of colonel at age
37. To compensate for his
weakened eyesight, he
always wore goggles
resembling swimming
goggles. It is said this
condition was a lingering
effect of torture
suffered when he was
taken prisoner by the
Principality of Zeon
during the One Year War.
His personality was cruel
and merciless toward
anyone outside the
Titans, especially
Spacenoids. He used poison
gas against colonies and
took hostages to recover
the Gundam Mk-II,
stopping at nothing to
achieve his goals. He was
truly a man who
symbolized the Titans.
Even after Jamitov's
assassination by Scirocco,
he attempted to resist
independently, but was
betrayed and destroyed
along with the Dogos Gear
by Yazan's Hambrabi,
vanishing into the void of
space.

Jamaican Daninghan was
an officer of the Titans
and Basque's close
confidant. His rank was
major. He was of a
superior class as a
commander, but he was a
believer in elitist
ideology and had an
arrogant personality. In
reality, however, he was
a coward who only
watched his superiors'
expressions, and so it
seemed he did not enjoy
the trust of his
subordinates.

Jamaican Daningan was a
subordinate of Basque,
who commanded the
Titans, serving as his
adjutant with the rank of
major. He was a capable
commander, but he held
elitist beliefs and an
arrogant personality. In
reality, however, he was
a coward who only
watched his superior's
mood, and as a result he
did not enjoy the trust
of his subordinates. His
end was also miserable:
Yazan, who found his
existence troublesome, set
him up, and a Super
Gundam piloted by Emma,
guided by the deception,
struck his ship's bridge
directly.

Jamitov Hymem is a
founding member of the
Titans and its current
supreme commander,
holding the rank of
General. He is a
dangerous man who, while
hostile toward Spacenoids,
even considers purging
the Earthnoids who
pollute the Earth. He
made the Titans his own
personal tool for this
purpose, but it is ironic
that those who
disapproved of his
high-handed methods
joined forces and gave
rise to the AEUG, his
greatest obstacle. He had
long been at odds with
the AEUG leader Blex as a
political rival. While
having his confidant
Basque command the
Titans, he deliberately
released the dangerous
element Scirocco within
the organization to stir
up activity.

death was used by
Scirocco to seize control
of the Titans.

Gady Kinsey is an
officer of the Titans and
captain of the cruiser
Alexandria. He is a
soldier's soldier who
values discipline, and his
meticulous nature leads
him to speak his mind
even to superiors if they
overstep their authority.

Gady Kinsey is an

captain of the cruiser
Alexandria. He is a
soldier's soldier who
values discipline, and his
meticulous nature leads
him to speak his mind
even to superiors if they
overstep their authority.

Wong Lee is an executive
of Anaheim Electronics.
Entrusted with full
authority by the
company's chairman,
Melanie, he is the man
monitoring the AEUG
aboard the Argama.
Compared to the TV
version, where he left a
strong impression of
correcting Kamille and the
others at every turn, in
the theatrical version he
is portrayed as a strict
but composed adult.

Blex Forer is the
representative of the
anti-Earth Federation
organization AEUG, holding
the rank of Commodore.
At 58 years old, he was
a high-ranking official of
the Earth Federation
Forces and a member of
the Earth Federation
Assembly, but concerned
over the rise of the
Titans and policies that
disregarded the Earth's
environment, he organized
the AEUG. He was a man
of gentle character with
a flexible mindset that
showed understanding even
toward Newtypes, and he
held high hopes for
Kamille.

Blex Forer was the
leader of the Anti-Earth
Union Group, holding the
rank of commodore at age
58. A high-ranking officer
of the Earth Federation
Forces and a member of
the Federation Congress,
he organized the AEUG
out of concern over the
rise of the Titans and
policies that disregarded
the Earth's environment.
He had a gentle
personality and flexible
thinking that included
understanding of
Newtypes, and he placed
expectations on Kamille as
well. While attending the
Federation Congress in
Dakar, he was
assassinated by Jamitov's
machinations, and with his
dying breath entrusted
his legacy to Quattro,
who carried on the will
of Zeon.

Henken Bekkener is a
central figure of the
AEUG, holding the rank of
Lieutenant Colonel. He was
the first captain of the
Argama, but upon Bright's
joining of the AEUG, he
yielded that position and
became captain of the
Radish. Though he had
spent many years in the
military, he retained a
certain human warmth
that endeared him to his
crew. He had also
participated in the One
Year War and was said to
have felt the pressure of
the Red Comet on the
battlefield. He harbored
feelings for Emma and
often showed a sincere,
boyish side.

Henken Bekkener was a
central figure of the
AEUG, holding the rank of
Lieutenant Commander. He
was the first captain of
the Argama, but when
Bright joined the AEUG,
he handed over that post
and became the captain
of the Radish. Although
he had spent many years
in the military, he
retained a certain human
warmth that endeared him
to his crew, who trusted
him deeply. He had also
participated in the One
Year War and claimed to
have felt the pressure of
the Red Comet on the
battlefield. He harbored
feelings of affection for
Emma and often showed a
pure-hearted side around
her. During the final
battle against the Titans,
in order to protect
Emma's Gundam Mk-II
which had fallen into a
dire situation, he used
the Radish as a shield
and shared his fate with
the ship as it was blown
apart.

Astonaige Medoz serves
as the chief mechanic of
the Argama, holding the
rank of petty officer.
His skill is assured given
his position, and because
of him, the Argama's
mobile suit team is
always able to fight at
full readiness. In the TV
version, he sent Kamille's
ideas to Anaheim
Electronics, playing a
hidden role as a
contributor to the
completion of the Zeta
Gundam. However, this
aspect is not depicted in
the theatrical version.

Astonaige Medos was the
chief mechanic aboard the
Argama, holding the rank
of Sergeant. His skill was
as reliable as his position
suggested, and his
presence ensured that the
Argama's Mobile Suit
teams could always fight
at full readiness. In the
TV series, he was also an
unsung hero who sent
Kamille's concepts to
Anaheim Electronics,
playing a key role in the
completion of the Zeta
Gundam; however, this
aspect was not depicted
in the theatrical version.
His talents were evidently
well regarded, as he later
served as a mechanic
under Bright during the
Second Neo Zeon War.

Hayato Kobayashi is the
founder of Karaba, a
support organization for
the AEUG, and the captain
of the Audhumla. He had
been serving as the
director of a war museum
at Kennedy, but he rose
up after witnessing the
tyranny of the Titans.
During the One Year War,
he was a crew member of
the White Base, and after
the war ended, he married
Frau and adopted the
orphans Katz, Lets, and
Kikka.

Kai Shiden is ostensibly
a freelance journalist
(in his own words,
'little more than a
tabloid hack'). In
reality, however, he is a
collaborator who provides
information on the Titans
to the AEUG and Karaba.
During the One Year War,
he had fought alongside
Hayato on the White Base,
and he would investigate
the locations of
Federation headquarters
and relay them to Hayato.
Nevertheless, he shows
reluctance about fighting
together with Quattro,
knowing him to be Char.

Beltorchika Irma is a
member of Karaba, a
support organization for
the AEUG. She is an
energetic woman, but
because she has a
tendency to blurt out
whatever she thinks, she
often incurred the
resentment of those
around her. When she
made contact with the
Audhumla, she was
delighted to meet Amuro,
the hero of the One Year
War, in whom she had
been interested from
before. She soon repeated
intense overtures toward
him, and eventually came
to support the roused
Amuro as his lover.

Haman Karn is the
regent of the resource
asteroid Axis, where
remnants of the
Principality of Zeon's
military have gathered. In
practice, however, she is
the leader who commands
the entire force. Her
personality is fierce and
cold. Using Mineva, the
orphaned child of Gihren
Zabi, as her banner, she
proclaimed the revival of
Zeon and possessed the
high political acumen to
elevate Axis, once a
minor power, into a major
force. Her mobile suit
piloting skill and her
abilities as a Newtype are
also high, and she
sometimes takes to the
front lines herself in
dedicated machines such
as the Gaza C and the
Qubeley. She has a past
history with Quattro, and
harbors complex feelings
toward him that could be
called both love and
hatred.

Haman Karn was the
regent of Axis, a
resource asteroid where
remnants of the
Principality of Zeon's
military had gathered,
though in practice she
was the leader who
commanded the entire
force. Her personality was
fierce and cold-blooded.
Using Mineva, the
orphaned child of Dozle
Zabi, as her banner, she
championed the revival of
Zeon and possessed
considerable political
acumen, elevating the
weak Axis faction into a
major power. Her Mobile
Suit piloting skills and
abilities as a Newtype
were also exceptional, and
she sometimes took to
the front lines herself in
custom machines such as
the Gaza C and the
Qubeley. She had a past
history with Quattro and
held complex feelings
toward him that could be
called both love and
hatred. When Quattro's
Hyaku Shiki was consumed
in an explosion at the
end of their duel, she
murmured her feelings
aloud with a lonely air.

The late Vice Admiral of
the old Principality of
Zeon, Dozle Zabi's
orphaned child. Age 8.
 In her youth, she has
become a symbol of
Zeon's restoration
through the hands of her
guardian, Haman. However,
this is merely her
authority as a puppet of
Haman, and as a result,
she has received a rather
biased education.

A Moonrace boy who
pilots the Turn A Gundam.
Age 17.
 Along with Keith and
Fran, he descended to
Earth two years ago as
an advance surveyor for
the Earth return
operation. At that time,
he was saved from
drowning in a river by
the Heim sisters, and
through that connection
came to work at the Heim
family's mine, eventually
becoming a servant.
 He is gentle and dislikes
conflict, but in order to
stop the war between the
Moon and Earth, he
reluctantly joined the
Inglessa Militia.
 Contrary to his
personality, he excels at
piloting mobile suits, and
combined with the Turn A
Gundam's performance, he
played a central role in
the Militia. Also, even in
situations where he faced
enemies on foot without a
suit, he showed a manly
side, fighting bravely
without flinching.
 Like other Moonrace, he
was devoted to Dianna,
and his actions were
always prioritized with
Dianna in mind.

Loran Cehack was a
17-year-old boy of the
Moonrace and the pilot of
the Turn A Gundam. Along
with Keith and Fran, he
had descended to Earth
two years prior as an
advance scout for the
Earth Return Operation.
On that occasion, he was
saved from drowning in a
river by the Heim sisters,
and through that
connection he came to
work at the Heim family's
mine, eventually becoming
a servant. He had a
gentle disposition and
disliked conflict, but in
order to stop the war
between the Moon and
Earth, he reluctantly
joined the Inglessa
Militia. Despite his
personality, he was highly
skilled at piloting Mobile
Suits, and combined with
the performance of the
Turn A Gundam, he was a
core asset of the Militia.
In situations where he
faced enemies on foot
while armed, he also
showed a manly side,
fighting bravely without
hesitation. Like other
Moonrace, he was devoted
to Dianna, and her
well-being was always his
first priority in his
actions. After the final
confrontation with
Ghingnham, he stepped
into a new life together
with Dianna, who had
remained on Earth after
swapping places with
Kihel.

Loran's appearance
dressed as a woman.
 It was promoted through
Guin's scheme as the
pilot of the Turn A
Gundam, but it seems
that Guin's own personal
tastes came through more
strongly.
 Under Kihel's guidance,
thorough training as a
noble lady was conducted,
not just in appearance
but also in bearing and
dancing. Loran carried it
out admirably, even going
so far as to capture
Harry's heart (?).
 Although her appearances
in the main story were
few, she appeared every
time in the first opening
sequence.

The eldest daughter of
the Heim family, whom
Loran served as a
servant. Age 17.
 She was not bound by
feudal social conventions,
held the belief that
women should advance into
society, and served as
Guin's assistant.
 She resembled Dianna,
the Queen of the Moon,
so closely that even her
own family could not tell
them apart. At Dianna's
suggestion, they playfully
swapped places, but they
missed the timing to
switch back, and she
ended up truly placed in
the position of queen.
 However, this became a
turning point, as she
learned that the Moonrace
were no different from
Earthlings, and she began
to make efforts to
understand Dianna's
thinking and to consider
what she herself should
do.
 Harry, who was the first
to notice the swap,
risked his life to protect
her, and as they shared
the secret, she came to
harbor feelings for him.
The way she confessed
her love was that of a
girl her age.

Kihel Heim was the
eldest daughter of the
Heim family, for whom
Loran worked as a
servant, and was 17 years
old. Unbound by feudal
social conventions, she
believed that women
should advance into the
wider society, and she
served as an aide to
Guin. She bore such a
striking resemblance to
the Moon Queen Dianna
that even her own family
could not tell them apart.
At Dianna's suggestion,
they began swapping
places half in jest, but
the timing to switch back
was lost, and she ended
up truly placed in the
position of queen. That
turn of events led her to
realize that the Moonrace
were no different from
Earthlings, and she came
to strive to understand
Dianna's thinking and to
consider what she herself
should do. Harry, who was
the first to notice the
swap, protected her at
the risk of his own life,
and as they shared the
secret together, she came
to develop feelings for
him. When she confessed
her love, she appeared as
a girl of her age. After
peace was restored, she
swapped back with Dianna
and, before the Moonrace,
claimed the name Dianna.

The head of the Soreil
family that rules the
Moon, and the Queen of
the Moonrace.
 She is the spiritual
pillar of the Moonrace,
commanding overwhelming
trust and respect.
 Her official age is 19,
but having repeated
artificial hibernation many
times, several hundred
years seem to have
passed since her birth.
During that time, she has
visited Earth on several
occasions, and those
experiences became a
major driving force for
the return to Earth.
 Through a chance
occurrence, she met Kihel,
who had an identical
appearance, and out of
mischief, they swapped
places and lost the
opportunity to return to
their original positions.
But while living among
Earth's people as Kihel,
she came to hear their
true feelings and learned
about the true nature of
peace and how to achieve
it. And at last, she came
to know that her true
enemy to fight was
Agrippa.

Dianna Soreil is the
head of the Soreil family
that rules the Moon, and
the queen of the
Moonrace. She is the
emotional anchor for the
Moonrace, and commands
overwhelming trust and
respect. Her stated age
is 19, but due to
repeated artificial
hibernation, several
hundred years have passed
since her birth. During
that time she has visited
Earth several times, and
those experiences became
the major driving force
behind the return to
Earth. By chance she met
Kihel, who had an
identical appearance, and
while swapping places on
a whim, she lost the
opportunity to switch
back. However, while living
among Earth's people as
Kihel, she came to learn
their true feelings, and
learned about the true
nature of peace and how
to achieve it. And at
last, she came to know
that the true enemy she
must fight was Agrippa.
After defeating Agrippa
and Ghingnham, she
remained on Earth and
gained a happy life living
in nature alongside Loran.

Milan Rex served as a
governor who descended
to Earth alongside Dianna,
acting in a deputy-like
capacity. He was believed
to be a gentle and
intellectual man, but when
Phil rebelled in an
attempt to seize control
of the Dianna Counter,
Milan sided with the
military. This appeared to
be a painful decision made
to address various
problems, including the
slow-moving diplomacy and
food shortages. Loyalty
to Dianna remained rooted
deep in his heart, and
when Dianna returned to
Earth, he once again
became her subject.

Milan Rex was an
administrator who
descended to Earth with
Dianna, serving as a sort
of deputy. He seemed to
be a gentle and rational
person, but when Phil
rebelled in an attempt to
seize control of the
Dianna Counter, he sided
with the military. This
appeared to be a painful
decision made to deal
with various problems,
such as the slow-moving
diplomacy and food
shortages. Deep in his
heart, his loyalty to
Dianna remained rooted,
and when Dianna returned
to Earth, he once again
became her subject. After
the battle with
Ghingnham, he followed
Dianna (Kihel) and
returned to the Moon.

Sochie Heim was the
second daughter of the
Heim family, for whom
Loran worked as a
servant. She was 15 years
old. Her personality was
competitive, spirited, and
boyish. Although she was
concerned about Loran,
her own position and
temperament prevented her
from being honest about
her feelings. To avenge
her father, who died in
an attack by the Dianna
Counter, she volunteered
for the Inglessa Militia
and became a Kapool
pilot. Because of this,
she was initially hardened
with hatred toward the
Moonrace. However,
through learning Loran's
true identity and the
affair with Gavane, who
loved her and even
proposed to her, she grew
greatly as a person.

Sochie Heim is the
second daughter of the
Heim family, for whom
Loran worked as a
servant. She is 15 years
old. Her personality is
competitive, spirited, and
tomboyish. She is
interested in Loran, but
due to their positions
and her temperament, she
cannot be honest about
it. To avenge her father,
who was killed in an
attack by the Dianna
Counter, she volunteered
for the Inglessa Militia
and became a Kapool
pilot. Because of that,
she was initially hardened
with hatred toward the
Moonrace. But through
learning Loran's true
identity and the incident
with Gavane, who loved
her and even proposed to
her, she grew greatly as
a person. In the end, her
feelings for Loran were
never fulfilled, and she
exchanged a tearful
farewell kiss with Loran,
who chose to go with
Dianna. Afterwards, she
threw Loran's goldfish
toy into the river,
parting with her own
feelings.

Meschee Kun was born
into a family of airplane
makers that had run the
business since her
grandfather's generation,
and she herself flew
through the skies as an
airplane pilot. She was 18
years old. She belonged
to the Inglessa Militia's
airplane division and had
fought since the outbreak
of war. She had a
friendship that could be
called close with Sochie,
and after the Kapool was
excavated, the two often
rode into battle together.
When she went to the
Moon, she became friendly
with a boy soldier of the
Dianna Counter and
sortied together with him
in a WaD.

Meshee Kuhn was born
into a family of airplane
makers going back to her
grandfather's generation,
and she herself flies
through the sky as an
airplane pilot. She is 18
years old. She belonged
to the airplane unit of
the Inglessa Militia and
had been fighting since
the start of the war.
She and Sochie were close
enough to be called best
friends, and after the
Kapool was excavated,
they often rode into
battle together. When she
went up to the Moon, she
became friendly with a
boy soldier of the Dianna
Counter, and sortied
together with him in a
WaD. Her relationship with
this boy seems to have
continued even after the
war ended.

Corin Nander was a
sergeant in the Dianna
Counter. In the past, he
had been subjected to a
freezing sentence in a
military prison along with
his Eagail for the reason
that he had massacred 85
rebel elements who had
tried to kill Dianna
without holding a trial.
As his actions made
clear, his loyalty to
Dianna was twice as
strong as that of others.
He was released under the
pretext of a pardon to
participate in the Earth
Return Operation and
descended to Earth.
However, this was believed
to have been arranged by
Agrippa, who sought to
throw the front lines
into confusion by sending
the reckless Corin in. Due
to the freezing and
errors during thawing, his
hair had fallen out and
part of his face had
become altered, but it
was said that he had
originally been a handsome
man with blond hair. He
showed an abnormal
obsession and hostility
toward 'Gundam' and
continued to target the
Turn A Gundam.

had been subjected to a

military prison along with
his Eagail for the reason
that he had massacred 85
rebel elements who had

As his actions made

He was released under the

However, this was believed

Corin Nander was a
former sergeant of the
Dianna Counter. After
being defeated by Loran,
he entered the priesthood
and wandered the land,
but upon seeing the light
of the M-Fly released by
Merrybell's Turn A
Gundam, he remembered his
own mission. He then went
to Dianna, and when he
was permitted to return
to the military and to
destroy the Turn-type
Gundam, he was so
overcome with emotion
that he shed tears. His
unrestrained behavior,
such as having a Kapool
repainted in his own
private colors, continued
to astonish those around
him. However, his skill had
not declined, and he
performed aerial combat
in a Kapool, which should
have been unfamiliar to
him, overwhelming the
Mahiroo unit with his
exploits.

Corin Nander is a former
sergeant of the Dianna
Counter. After being
defeated by Loran, he
entered the priesthood
and wandered from place
to place, but when he
saw the light of the
M-Fly released by
Merrybell's Turn A
Gundam, he remembered his
own mission. He headed to
Dianna, and when he was
permitted to return to
the military and to
defeat the Turn-type
Gundam, he was so moved
that he wept. His
reckless behavior
continued as before, such
as having a Kapool
repainted in his own
custom colors, much to
the amazement of those
around him. But his skill
had not declined, and he
performed aerial combat
in the unfamiliar Kapool,
overwhelming the Mahiroo
unit. Eventually, when the
Turn X also activated its
M-Fly, he deliberately
stole fuel from the
Kapools of Sochie and
Meshee, leaving the two
of them far from the
battlefield, and went
alone to his death.

is a young man who
works on excavation
operations in the
Mountain Cycle as a
disciple of the prospector
Sid. He is 23 years old.
 He was born into the
minority Maban tribe, and
as a child his parents
were killed in tribal
warfare. He was abandoned
in the mountains and
taken in by Sid. Because
of this background, he
harbored a rivalry that
could be called hostility
toward the Northern
Ameliaans and the
Moonrace, and his
attitude toward Loran in
particular was harsh.
 His extensive knowledge
of machinery was
recognized, and he joined
the Militia's mobile suit
unit, where he came to
command the Jarapi (junk
car) squad.
 While riding in the Flat
that Loran and the
others used during their
descent to Earth, he
fought in it, and he
gradually developed a
close relationship with
Fran, who had taught him
how to pilot it.

Joseph Yott was a young
man of 23 who worked as
a disciple of the mountain
prospector Sid, involved
in excavation work at the
Mountain Cycle. He was
born into the minority
Maba tribe, and in his
childhood his parents were
killed in tribal conflict;
he was abandoned in the
mountains and taken in by
Sid. Because of this past,
he harbored a rivalry
that could be called
hostility toward North
Americans and Moonrace
alike, and his attitude
toward Loran was
especially harsh. His
abundant knowledge of
machinery was recognized,
and he joined the
Militia's mobile suit unit,
coming to command the
Jarapee (junk vehicle)
squad. While fighting
aboard the flat that
Loran and the others
used during their descent
to Earth, he grew close
to Fran, who had taught
him how to pilot it.
After peace came, he
seems to have quit the
prospector's trade for
the sake of his family,
and he was seen carrying
the child he had with
Fran while working hard
at his new job as a
fishmonger.

is an old man known as
a prospector, an
excavator, and also a
researcher of the Black
History.
 Together with his
disciple Joseph, he
excavates machines such
as the Kapool from the
Mountain Cycle. Through
his involvement in
commanding the excavation
of weapons, he came to
accompany the Militia.
 He showed vitality
beyond his years in many
places, dashing between
excavation sites without
sparing time for sleep,
and when manpower was
short, boarding a
Borjarnon to intercept
the enemy.
 His trademark was a
helmet with an attached
flashlight, reminiscent of
a frog, that seemed
convenient for excavation
work.

Sid Munza was an old
man called a mountain
prospector - an excavator
and also a researcher of
the Black History.
Together with his disciple
Joseph, he excavated
Kapools and other
artifacts from the
Mountain Cycle. Because
he had taken command of
excavating weapons, he
came to accompany the
Militia. He flew around
excavation sites without
sparing sleep, and when
manpower was short he
would board a Borjarnon
to intercept the enemy,
showing vitality beyond
his years in every scene.
His trademark was a
helmet with an attached
flashlight that made him
look like a frog and
seemed convenient for
excavation work. After
the fighting ended, he
returned to prospecting
with Poe, who appeared to
have been taken on as a
new disciple in place of
Joseph, who had started a
family.

is the grandson of the
lord of Inglessa and the
central figure of the
Inglessa Militia. He is 19
years old.
 Though raised as a
pampered young master, he
had no sense of being
naive about the world. He
showed shrewdness in
using whatever was
available to him, and
talent in negotiation,
politics, and judgment,
and these were further
honed through battle.
 Even when confronted
with the Moonrace's
overwhelming technology,
he was not crushed, but
instead secretly planned
to use that technology to
bring about an industrial
revolution. Even when
Inglessa fell and he lost
power, he resolved to
climb back up from there,
making him an ambitious
man with resilience.
 He had a strong fixation
on Loran, calling him
'Laura' and having him
dress in women's clothing.

Guin Sard Rheinford was
the grandson of the
Inglessa lord and a
central figure of the
Inglessa Militia. He was
19 years old. Though
raised as a young master,
he had no sense of being
naive about the world,
and showed a tenacity to
use whatever could be
used, along with excellent
negotiation skills,
political acumen, and
judgment, all of which
were further honed
through battle. Even when
confronted with the
Moonrace's overwhelming
technology, he was not
crushed, but instead
secretly planned to use
that technology to bring
about an industrial
revolution. Even when
Inglessa fell and he lost
power, he resolved to
climb back up from there
- an ambitious man with
resilience. He had a
strong fixation on Loran,
calling him 'Laura' and
making him dress in
women's clothing. Even
when he betrayed Dianna,
he tried to bring only
Loran over to his side,
and this obsession went
somewhat beyond the
bounds of reason. In the
epilogue, he was confirmed
to have crossed to Gallia
together with Merrybell,
whom he had saved with
his own hands.

is the commander of the
Inglessa Militia. His rank
is colonel. He is 35 years
old.
 He believes that the
Moonrace are invaders of
Earth and that the fight
against them is a matter
of defending his homeland.
For this reason, he
seemed displeased with
Guin, whom he considered
a mere figurehead and
who viewed war as nothing
more than one means of
negotiation.
 However, he was swept
along by the rapidly
changing situation and by
Guin's resourcefulness in
forming strategies to
match, and in the end he
followed him all the way
to the final battle.

Michael Guern was the
commander of the Inglessa
Militia, with the rank of
colonel. He was 35 years
old. He believed that the
Moonrace were invaders of
Earth and that fighting
them was a matter of
defending his homeland.
For this reason, he
seemed displeased that
Guin, whom he considered
a mere figurehead, viewed
the war as nothing more
than one means of
negotiation. However, he
was tossed about by the
rapidly changing situation
and by Guin's drive in
formulating strategies to
match it, and in the end
he followed along all the
way to the final battle.
But when the Willgem
crashed down and Guin's
ambitions came to an end,
he at the same time
abandoned him and went
his own way.

Gavane Gooney is the
captain of the Suisai
Squad, the elite mobile
suit unit of the Rujana
Militia. He is 27 years
old.
 He has a cheerful
personality, but on the
battlefield he is a fierce
commander who always
leads from the front,
earning him deep trust
from his subordinates. He
thinks flexibly, changing
tactics to suit the
situation.
 When he first met the
Inglessa Militia, he
treated Loran and the
others with contempt,
calling them 'Inglessa
bastards' and challenging
the Turn A Gundam to a
test of strength. But as
they fought together, he
came to acknowledge them
as comrades in arms. In
particular, he was drawn
to Sochie, whom he called
'little miss,' by her
earnest way of fighting,
and he eventually went so
far as to propose to her.

Gavane Gooney was the
captain of the Sue Sai Do
squad, the elite mobile
suit unit of the Luzan
Militia. He was 27 years
old. He had a cheerful
personality, but on the
battlefield he was a
valiant commander who
always led from the
front, earning deep trust
from his subordinates. He
had a flexible mind,
changing tactics to suit
the situation. When he
first met the Inglessa
Militia, he treated Loran
and the others with
derision, calling them
'Inglessa bastards' and
challenging the Turn A
Gundam to a test of
strength. But as they
fought together, he came
to acknowledge them as
comrades in arms. In
particular, he was drawn
to Sochie, whom he called
'young miss', by her
single-minded way of
fighting, and he went so
far as to propose to her.
However, while fighting
the Red squad in the
underground tunnels of
Lost Mountain over the
excavated nuclear bomb,
he vanished into the light
of a nuclear blast that
went off by accident.
Every one of his comrades
mourned his death and
shed tears.

Lily Borjarnon is the
13th and youngest
daughter of Duke
Borjarnon, the lord of
the Lujane domain. Her
personality is selfish and
naive, and her carefree
attitude of not
understanding war is
exactly that of a young
lady. However, her insight
into matters and her
observational ability to
judge a person's true
nature are extraordinary.
She has known Guin since
childhood, and there were
scenes where she
harassed Kihel (Dianna)
for approaching him.
However, she eventually
came to admire Kihel, who
served as Queen of the
Moon in Dianna's place,
and offered to become
her friend.

Lili Borjano is the
thirteenth and youngest
daughter of Duke Borjano,
lord of Rujan. Her
personality is selfish and
naive about the world,
and her lighthearted
inability to comprehend
war is just like a young
lady of privilege. However,
she possesses
extraordinary insight into
matters and keen
observational skills for
judging a person's true
character. She had known
Guin since childhood, and
was seen harassing Kihel,
who was acting as Dianna,
when she approached him.
Eventually, however, she
came to admire Kihel, who
served as Queen of the
Moon in Dianna's place,
and offered to become
her friend. When she was
betrayed by Guin, she
showed no sign of being
shaken, and instead
displayed a strong core
by attempting to stop his
actions. She once even
proposed to Loran, saying
'Become Laura and seduce
Guin.' This may have been
a reflection of her
wounded heart, stemming
from being disregarded as
a woman.

Horace Niven is a
Moonrace engineer.
Initially he acted
alongside the Dianna
Counter that accompanied
him, but he defected to
Earth, driven by his
intellectual curiosity
toward the excavated
Earth weapons.
Thereafter, at Guin's
request, he came to
cooperate with the
Inglessa Militia. There
were many places where
he could demonstrate his
abilities, such as the
research, analysis, repair,
and maintenance of
excavated weapons
including the Turn A
Gundam. Although most
Earthlings did not look
favorably upon the
Moonrace engineers, they
seemed not to care much,
perhaps because they
were only interested in
unknown technology. He
had a distinctive face
like a Great Buddha
statue, and Merrybell,
whose face resembled a
panda's, told him he had
an 'amusing face.'

Horace Nyben is a
Moonrace engineer.
Initially he worked
alongside the Dianna
Counter that had
accompanied him, but he
defected to Earth, driven
by his intellectual
curiosity toward the
excavated Earth weapons.
Afterwards, at Guin's
request, he came to
cooperate with the
Inglessa Militia. There
were many places where
he could demonstrate his
abilities, including the
research, analysis, repair,
and maintenance of
excavated weapons such
as the Turn A Gundam.
Although most Moonrace
engineers were not
well-regarded by
Earthlings, he seemed not
to care much, perhaps
because he was only
interested in unknown
technology. He had a
distinctive face like a
great Buddha statue, and
Merrybell, who had a
panda-like face, called it
an 'interesting face.'
After the war ended, he
remained on Earth and
helped with the
restoration of the
Willgem.

Harry Ord serves as
captain of the Dianna
Counter's elite guard. He
is 18 years old and holds
the rank of lieutenant.
His personality is calm
and intellectual, but
because he is overly
earnest, he also has an
inflexible side. He has
sworn absolute loyalty to
Dianna, and the depth of
his devotion is so famous
that even an ordinary
female soldier knows of
it. He was the first to
notice the swap between
Dianna and Kihel, but he
continued to serve
without changing his
attitude and protected
Kihel. He always wears
red sunglasses, which are
night-vision goggles, and
according to him, they
serve to 'hide his gaze
when looking at women
other than Dianna.' He did
not even remove them
when kissing Kihel, who
had developed feelings for
him, but it seems he was
not disliked for that. His
skill piloting his
gold-colored custom SUMO
is top-class. At the
Winter Palace, he took on
the Mahiroo squad led by
Sweatson and defeated
them in seconds with a
single unit, which shows
his true ability. He
favored suits and vests
in a yellow-and-black
combination, and pajamas
with star marks, leaving
his fashion sense open to
question.

Harry Ord serves as the
captain of the Dianna
Guard. He is 18 years old
and holds the rank of
lieutenant, later being
promoted to captain. His
personality is calm and
intellectual, but he is
too earnest, giving him an
inflexible side. He has
sworn absolute loyalty to
Dianna, and his devotion
is so famous that even
ordinary female soldiers
know of it. He was the
first to notice the
switch between Dianna and
Kiel, but he continued to
serve without changing
his attitude, and
protected Kihel. He always
wears red sunglasses that
serve as night-vision
goggles, which he himself
says are 'to hide his
gaze when looking at
women other than Dianna.'
He did not even remove
them when kissing Kihel,
who had developed
feelings for him, but it
seems this did not cause
her to fall out of favor
with him. His skill in
piloting his gold-colored
custom SUMO is superbly
top-class. At the Winter
Palace, he took on the
Mahiroo unit led by
Suesson with a single
machine and defeated
them in seconds, which
shows his true ability. He
favored wearing
yellow-and-black suits
and vests, and pajamas
with star patterns,
leaving his fashion sense
questionable. After the
battle with Ghingnham
ended, and Kiel once again
switched places with
Dianna and crossed to the
Moon, Harry was at her
side as always.

Meme Midgard is a
Moonrace who infiltrated
Earth on Agrippa's orders.
His rank is captain. While
serving as the manager of
Keith's bread factory as
a cover, he plotted the
assassination of Dianna
and the seizure of the
Turn A Gundam. He had a
sly and suspicious
personality, and when he
judged that Teteth, whom
he had ordered to
assassinate Dianna, had
failed her mission, he
shot her dead to silence
her. The marksmanship he
displayed at that time
was considerable.
Furthermore, after
returning to the Moon, he
resorted to outrageous
acts such as fighting a
battle that involved the
Winter Palace, where many
citizens were in cryogenic
sleep. However, that
action became the trigger
for activating the M-Fly.

Meem Midgard is a
Moonrace who infiltrated
Earth on Agrippa's orders,
holding the rank of
captain. While serving as
the manager of Keith's
bread factory as a cover,
he plotted the
assassination of Dianna
and the seizure of the
Turn A Gundam. His
personality is sullen and
suspicious, and when he
judged that Teteth, who
had been ordered to
assassinate Dianna, had
failed her mission, he
shot her dead to silence
her. The marksmanship he
displayed at that time
was considerable. After
returning to the Moon, he
committed outrages such
as engaging in battle
involving the Winter
Palace, where many
citizens were in cryogenic
sleep. However, these
actions became the
trigger for activating the
M-Fly. In the end, he
shot his superior Agrippa,
and was then killed by
the hand of Harry's SUMO,
receiving 'the judgment of
Dianna's law.'

Teteth Halleh is a woman
who plotted to
assassinate Dianna under
Midgard's orders. She was
born between a Moonrace
and a woman whom Dianna
had once brought back
from Earth to the Moon.
Because she was raised
with discrimination from a
young age, she harbored
intense hatred toward
everything around her,
including Dianna, the lunar
system, and her Earthling
blood. As a reward for
the assassination, she had
secured a promise from
Midgard to make her an
honorary citizen of the
Moon.

Teteth Halle is a woman
who plotted the
assassination of Dianna
on Midgard's orders. She
was born to a woman
Dianna had brought back
from Earth to the Moon,
and a Moonrace man.
Having grown up facing
discrimination from an
early age, she harbored
intense hatred toward
everything around her -
Dianna, the Moon's
system, and Earthling
blood. As a reward for
the assassination, she had
secured a promise from
Midgard to make her an
honorary citizen of the
Moon. The plan failed,
however, and she was
shot dead by Midgard, who
feared the matter would
come to light. Later, a
scene was broadcast
showing her mother Linda
waking from cryogenic
sleep and searching for
her daughter, which only
emphasized the tragedy
further.

Phil Ackermann was a
lieutenant in the Dianna
Counter and became the
commander of the Earth
descent operation after
the death of his
predecessor. He looked
down on Earthlings as
barbarians and advocated
for subjugation by force.
However, taking advantage
of Dianna's departure
from Earth while she
sought peaceful
coexistence, he rose in
rebellion and declared the
founding of the Sunbelt
Republic. At one point he
even displayed the
ambition of becoming the
king of Earth, but in the
end he swore his loyalty
to Dianna once again. He
then united with the
Earth side, despite
lingering ill feelings, and
fought against the
Ghingnham fleet.

Phil Ackman was a
lieutenant in the Dianna
Counter. After the death
of his senior officer, he
became the commander of
the Earth descent
operation. He looked down
on Earthlings as
barbarians and advocated
for subjugation by
military force. However,
taking advantage of
Dianna's departure from
Earth due to her desire
for peaceful coexistence,
he turned traitor and
declared the founding of
the Sunbelt Republic. At
one point he even showed
ambition to become the
king of Earth, but in the
end he swore loyalty to
Dianna once more. He then
united even with the
Earth side, which still
harbored ill feelings, and
fought against the
Ghingnham fleet. After
the fighting was over, he
returned to the Moon
together with Dianna
(Kihel) and the others.

Poe Eiji was a lieutenant
in the Dianna Counter.
She descended to Earth
as a pilot of a Wodom
under Phil's command. Her
interception of the
Militia's airplane forces
became the opening of
the long conflict between
Earth and the Moon. She
was quick to tears,
weeping at every turn,
and her tearfulness even
became the subtitle of
episode 31. She appears
to have been in a
romantic relationship with
her superior Phil, and she
followed him when he
rebelled against Dianna.
Yet, deep in her heart,
her loyalty to the queen
remained rooted, and when
Dianna returned, she wept
tears of joy.

Poe Eiji was a second
lieutenant in the Dianna
Counter. She descended to
Earth as a pilot of a
Wodom under Phil's
command. Her interception
of the Militia's airplane
squadron became the
opening of the
long-standing conflict
between Earth and the
Moon. She was quick to
tears and wept at every
turn, and this tearfulness
even became the subtitle
of episode 31. She
appeared to be in a
romantic relationship with
her superior Phil, and she
followed him when he
raised his banner of
rebellion against Dianna.
Yet deep in her heart,
loyalty to the Queen was
rooted, and when Dianna
returned she once again
shed tears of joy. After
all the battles were over,
she could be seen taking
on Mountain Cycle
alongside Sid, perhaps
having become his
apprentice.

Ghingnham Gym was the
head of the Ghingnham
family, which governed the
martial arts of the
Moonrace, and the supreme
commander of the
Ghingnham space fleet.
True to his words that
'battle itself is my
reason for existence,' he
always carried a sword
and personally boarded
the Turn X to go to the
front lines. This behavior
stemmed from his intense
pride in being a man of
the warrior class.
Ordinarily he held a calm
and broad-minded view,
but once battle began, he
revealed his arrogant and
belligerent nature. As a
result, he would become
so excited that he lost
sight of his surroundings
and would attack friend
and foe alike, exposing
his battle mania. His
greatest reason for
opposing Dianna was his
resentment that she had
organized the Dianna
Counter on her own and
descended to Earth,
ignoring those like himself
who had spent 2,500
years repeating drills.
Conversely, this also
proved that he held
strong loyalty toward
Dianna.

Ghingnham Gym was the
head of the Ghingnham
family, which governed the
martial arts of the
Moonrace, and the supreme
commander of the
Ghingnham space fleet.
True to his words,
'Combat is the very
reason for my existence,'
he always carried a sword
and personally boarded
the Turn X to go to the
front lines. This behavior
stemmed from his intense
pride in being a man of
the warrior class. Usually
he was calm and held
broad-minded views, but
once battle began, he
revealed his arrogant and
belligerent true nature.
As a result, he became so
excited that he lost
sight of his surroundings,
exposing his battle mania
by attacking friend and
foe alike without
distinction. The greatest
reason he opposed Dianna
was his resentment that
she had ignored him and
his people, who had
repeated exercises for
2500 years, and had
independently organized
the Dianna Counter to
descend to Earth.
Conversely, this also
served as proof of his
strong loyalty to Dianna.
Against Loran's Turn A
Gundam, which he
recognized as his sworn
enemy, he fought to a
draw even in the final
battle, with both machines
destroyed. Mere moments
after escaping, he then
faced Loran in personal
combat with swords, but
during that struggle he
was swallowed by the
cocoon of the Moonlight
Butterfly and returned to
the Earth along with the
two Turn-type machines.

Sweatson Sterro was the
captain leading the
Mahiroo squad of the
Ghingnham fleet. He was
rough in temperament,
vulgar in character, and
casually imposed
unreasonable demands on
his subordinates.
Midgard's assessment of
him as 'a water blister
leaning on the prestige
of a distinguished family'
was apt, as he was a man
full of flaws. His fighting
style also lacked
flexibility, as he could
only perform formulaic
movements due to having
conducted nothing but
drills within the fleet.

Suesson Stello was the
captain leading the
Mahiroo squadron of the
Ghingnham fleet. He was a
man full of faults:
rough in personality, base
in character, and calmly
imposing unreasonable
demands on his
subordinates. It was no
wonder Midgard described
him as 'a water blister
riding on the prestige of
a distinguished family.'
His fighting style was
also lacking in flexibility,
as he could only perform
by-the-book maneuvers
due to having done
nothing but drills within
the fleet. His end was a
pitiful one: he cut into
a battle between
Turn-type machines,
incurred Ghingnham's
wrath, and was shot down
by him.

Merrybell Gadget was a
girl said to be
Ghingnham's puppet. She
came from the lowest
class of the Moon and
had been picked up by
Ghingnham in the past.
Her appearance - a
bizarre outfit that also
served as a spacesuit,
large earmuffs, eye
makeup, and bells on her
head - along with her
agility, such as
performing handstands
even on Earth with its
six times the Moon's
gravity, evoked the image
of a clown. She preferred
to be near capable and
amusing individuals such
as Ghingnham and Guin,
and she would throw out
words and actions that
incited war toward them.
Despite what her
demeanor suggested, she
possessed exceptional
mobile suit piloting skill
and maneuvered the Bandit
as if it were an
extension of her own
limbs. Her coordination
with unmanned mobile
suits seemed to rely on a
special ability she
possessed, but the details
remained unknown.

Agrippa Maintener is the
head of the Maintener
family, which has managed
the Winter Palace, the
artificial hibernation
facility of the Moonrace.
As the administrative
official in charge of the
internal affairs of
Ghingnham, the capital of
the Moon, he is
well-versed in the Turn A
Gundam and the Black
History.
 He had set the
maintenance of tranquility
and peace in lunar
society as his supreme
objective, and feared
that contact with
Earthlings would awaken
the instinct for conflict
in the hearts of the
Moonrace. For this reason,
he opposed the Earth
descent operation, and
carried out various acts
of sabotage, such as
delaying supplies and
plotting the assassination
of Dianna.

Keith Laijie is a
Moonrace youth of 17 who
descended to Earth two
years ago along with
Loran and Fran as an
advance surveyor for the
return to Earth.
 He was working as an
apprentice at the Donkey
bakery in Nox. However,
when the Dianna Counter
descended, he took over
the shop along with the
master's daughter Berlune
after the master was
injured.
 He sold the flat he had
used during the descent
to the Inglessa Militia,
used the money to build a
bread factory, and
actively hired Moonrace
who had fled. This
positive attitude of doing
his best at what he could
do greatly contributed to
bridging Earth and the
Moon at the civilian level.
 Whether as a result of
his efforts or not, his
bread-making skill was
excellent, and its taste
was highly praised by
both Earthlings and
Moonrace alike.

Fran Doll is a Moonrace
girl of 17 who descended
to Earth two years ago
along with Loran and
Keith as an advance
surveyor for the return
to Earth.
 She worked as a printer
at the Nox Chronicle, a
Nox newspaper company,
but later became a
newspaper reporter,
fulfilling her long-held
wish. She always
considered the
significance of reporting
and tried to convey the
truth without flinching
even in the face of war.
Even when she learned
that her articles were
being suppressed by media
controls, she did not
abandon her duties as a
reporter.
 She came to know Joseph
through a chance
encounter, and eventually
became close enough to
speak her true feelings
and act dependent in
front of him.

Garrod Ran is a boy of
15 who survives in the
devastated world by his
own strength without
relying on others.
 He is a war orphan, but
has a bright and
forward-looking
personality that shows no
sense of tragedy. Perhaps
because his father was a
military scientist, he is
skilled in handling
machinery in general.
Behind that may have
been a desire to become
an engineer like his
father. Before boarding
the Freeden, he used his
natural resourcefulness
and cunning to hunt
Mobile Suits and sell them
to junk dealers, living
toughly. Perhaps learned
from such a life, he once
opened the locks of the
Freeden and the Bradman
residence using only wire.
 His Mobile Suit piloting
skill was genius-level, and
he quickly mastered the
Gundam X and the Gundam
Double X on his first
flights. Even in his first
battle in space, he
grasped the knack in an
extremely short time.
Lancelow, who witnessed
his high adaptability,
could not hide his
astonishment.
 During a certain job, he
met the Newtype girl
Tiffa and fell in love at
first sight. From then on,
he continued to show
single-minded devotion,
plunging into fire, water,
sea, or space without
regard for danger if it
was for her sake.
 Though self-proclaimed,
the epithet 'Pilot of the
Flaming Mobile Suit'
accurately describes him,
for better or worse.

Tiffa Adill is a
naturally awakened
Newtype girl of 15, born
after the 7th Space War,
who was whispered to be
impossible. She exhibits
powers that could be
called psychic abilities,
such as future sight,
danger detection, and
heightened perception
(the Newtypes of
'Gundam X' differ in
meaning from the
Newtypes of previous
Gundam series).
 Many organizations
targeted her as research
material for these
abilities, and she was
rescued by Jamil and the
others from confinement
in a Newtype research
facility. After boarding
the Freeden, she became
the group's guide and
ultimately reached the
D.O.M.E. on the Moon.
 Although her Newtype
abilities were sought
after by those around
her, she herself feared
them. She also detested
people fighting over this
power, and so lived with
her heart half-closed.
However, she gradually
opened up to Garrod, who
treated her as an
ordinary girl, and
eventually came to
express her feelings
outwardly.
 In the midst of battle,
she wished to be of help
to Garrod and other
precious people, and the
power heightened by that
feeling became a factor
in opening the D.O.M.E. on
the Moon.

Jamil Neate is the
captain of the Freeden, a
ship dedicated to the
search and protection of
Newtypes. He is 30 years
old.
 In addition to not
showing his emotions, the
sunglasses he always
wears give him an even
more taciturn impression.
However, the crew of the
Freeden place immense
trust in their captain,
revealing his human charm.
 During the 7th Space
War, he belonged to the
Earth Federation Forces
and was a Newtype who
served as the pilot of
the Gundam X. But in the
final phase of the war,
he pulled the trigger that
became the catalyst for
the greatest tragedy in
human history, the 'Colony
Drop'. That guilt became
a trauma, and he lost all
of his Newtype abilities.
 He suffered from a fear
of cockpits that
developed from his
trauma, but he overcame
it through his encounter
with Garrod. Thereafter,
he piloted the Gundam X
Divider and played an
active role.

Sara Tyrrell is the
operator of the Freeden.
She is 18 years old.
 She is a woman in a
vice-captain position who
sometimes serves as
acting captain when Jamil
is absent.
 She takes a theoretical
approach to thinking and
acts accordingly, but at
times she could not
suppress her own emotions
and would speak harshly.
 She harbors feelings
beyond respect for Jamil,
and when it comes to him,
she cannot remain calm.
She was also seen showing
jealousy toward Tiffa,
who was still a girl.
Amidst that, Roybea made
advances toward her, and
she found herself torn
between him and Jamil.
